Continuing session "Orchestrate cockpit fleet work" (instance 23cb5219-f410-4369-83d2-2e1d1fa3e6a7, claude, claude-opus-5-5, in /home/bewinxed/cockpit).

Before acting, run `git status` and `git diff --stat` to confirm the current state; the summary below may be stale.

## Summary of the session before its last turns
## Goal and constraints

This session is the orchestrator for CawCo. The repo is /home/bewinxed/cockpit and the hub runs on obelisk-of-light (machine d04ca118428001f1). The Mac is Omars-MacBook-Pro (271a214a5d568e4c). The work today: get previews working for the owner, ship the nightly and TestFlight, harden the release pipeline, and fix every bug that came up along the way.

**First step for the next session:** confirm you run on the host. `cat /proc/1/cmdline | tr '\0' ' ' | head -c 60` must not start with `bwrap`, and `systemctl --user is-active cawco-hub` must answer. This session was stuck inside Caw's lead sandbox (`bwrap --new-session --die-with-parent --unshare-net …`) after an account switch. Sessions started from `/home/bewinxed/cockpit` were also matched to Caw's place `6c2bfe58-caw`. Host work therefore went through sessions started with `cwd` `~/.config` (/home/bewinxed/.config), which really were on the host (`/sbin/init splash`).

Standing owner rules, verbatim where short:
- "if there's an honest caveat that you are aware of and you're just reporting it to me instead of fixing it, then your work is not done yet". The rule hook repeats it often.
- "I don't want the quick fix, I want the robust fix". No fallbacks without authorization. No unit tests. Cutover, with no shims. iOS parity.
- UI changes go advisor (Fable) → preview → owner pick → build. A UI brief carries interface-craft critique and Solar duotone icons. Don't list preview picks as "waiting on you" when the owner can't open them.
- Release check: "anything more than 1 minute is too much", "1 minute doesn't mean 1 minute", and "the code itself proves the fact". Speed things up by trimming, not tuning.
- "why do we keep a test suite that we have redesigned and rejected running at all": no old stage-2 wrappers.
- "if we're removing firecrawl WHY DO U NEED TO MENTION IT AT ALL?": no history lines in config.
- Never use claude-in-chrome. Never store or reuse the sudo password the owner pasted (he was told to rotate it). Kill only your own PIDs. Web access is CRW (`mcp__crw__crw_scrape`/`crw_map`/`crw_crawl`) plus Exa for search. Fleet config changes only through the admin_* tools. Don't touch the owner's model caches or another person's folder.
- On delegate briefs: anything touching apps/apple or openapi gets a Mac compile check. A UI brief gets interface-craft. A screenshot review runs on Sonnet as `browser`.

## Decisions and reasons

- **Firecrawl → CRW.**
  - CRW lives in compose project `crw` in ~/crw, bound to 127.0.0.1:3020. Tunnel `crw` 0175d099… serves crw.bewinxed.com, and the CF Access app "CRW" (aud 75227d5f…) has OAuth/DCR enabled. Claude Desktop connects to `https://crw.bewinxed.com/mcp`.
  - Fleet MCP `crw` was added and `firecrawl` removed. The fleet CLAUDE.md now names CRW and Exa only. The firecrawl services are disabled.
  - Exa stays for search, because SearXNG gets captcha'd.
- **Previews.**
  - The hub runs in host mode with pattern `https://p-{port}.bewinxed.com`, set via admin_previews_write once 3167 was live.
  - `p-*.bewinxed.com` was removed from CF Access app "Outpost" (4d48441a-0e08-4b24-8ab9-7df50265158c); the backup is at `~/.local/state/cf-backup/outpost-before.json`.
  - Previews now authenticate with hub-vouched tickets. `https://p-3457.bewinxed.com/` → 401 hub lock page. outpost.bewinxed.com still sends a 302 to Access.
  - Reason: the owner said "i'm not going to sign in per tab dude".
- **Release check rework (be50c3fe).**
  - 54 checks became 22 kept checks in 17 parallel rigs, with a proof-only clock and 3 builds instead of 12. release.ts runs stage 2 itself.
  - Fixes landed along the way:
    - `pids.peak` replaces `pids.current` (fa052bcb6). The kernel's `pids_try_charge` adds the charge before checking it, so `pids.current` reads limit+1 for an instant.
    - Fixed image-store run root (2adc7fed4). I fixed the db path in 77b6885a0, and in 0b6bddb32 storage now comes from storage.conf only, because `--root/--runroot/--storage-driver` drop the additional image store.
    - 67e5c09f8: KeyringMode=inherit, inotify admission, agent reconnect.
    - 76b8ec144: join_machine calls `$here/stage2-answer-prompts.py`.
    - f99cfdc21: apply_starts returns 0 when apply.log is missing.
    - bf44793ea: release.ts serializes holder.json writes (an ENOENT rename race).
  - Result: stage 2 takes 1021 s, 27/27 PASS.
- **Wire guard.**
  - TestFlight builds are recorded as git tags (`testflight-ios-<build>`), not in shipped-builds.json. shipped.ts reads origin's tags via `git ls-remote` (2712f5439).
  - App-facing breaks get no WIRE_PROTOCOL escape (638abfb14).
  - The `host` preview bridge stays while 20261015 is installable. I pushed tag `testflight-ios-20261015` at b324c0f29 and reverted the removal 809f69fba with e8a997dd4.
  - `routineMade` is a bridged field beside `event:null` until 20261015 expires.
- **MachinePath** (312b43065 etc., migration 0168 agents.home): one constructor resolves `~` against the machine's reported home or refuses; the hub DB's tilde rows were fixed. The place path is plain `string` on the wire again (4c80e6ddc).
- **Apple compile gate** (4dfa69070, migration 0172; fixes 325566142, c11584b0d): a project setting, on for cockpit (`cockpit|1`). Any item touching `apps/apple/**` or `scripts/lib/heavy-run.sh` gets a Mac `build-both.sh ios --compile-only` check. With no Mac online, the item waits via wait_item.
- **Formatting and typecheck tooling.**
  - Typecheck runs in parallel with svelte-check `--tsgo-experimental-api`, an openapi hash gate and 23 checks: about 9 s (9848b800f, b94e32ccb).
  - `bun fmt` comes from the pinned canary `@oven/bun-<platform>@1.4.3-canary.20261014.1` via scripts/fmt.ts (e67fad3b8, 98de6e580, c09c4a28f).
  - Biome `useSortedAttributes` is off for `**/*.svelte`, following the Prettier "integrating with linters" practice. The 14 `class:x` toggles became class expressions (biome#11281).
  - oxlint, bun lint and svelte-check-native were not adopted.
- **Other landed fixes:**
  - quiet/passive replacement pushes (99b45a50a);
  - failed or stopped attempts are not Needs-you, and a queued start keeps its origin (a738f7827, b428deb9d);
  - Caw asks show who, where and why, and read-only lines run ungated (2a4808be8);
  - routine origin and announce (eb1bd4223, 0169);
  - thread streaming plus typed not-woken plus a re-wake route (81cb1ef6d, 0170);
  - thread messages carry images and attachments (5f105635f, 0171);
  - internal drags never type into fields, and a file drop attaches (62f7a577a, b4d7f2b70);
  - delegates' screenshots are showable (56778ed84, c3a91caf1);
  - account move waits a bounded 2 min, and a person's session never resumes in a lead's place (bfc164309, bf1abb9fd);
  - OpenCode 2.0.29 pin with `shell` action names and permission.assert (052a10f2b);
  - transcripts tolerate NUL damage (44fd2e304). This session's transcript line 6450 has 1651 NULs, from an unclean stop on Oct 14.
  - TestFlight upload lock uses fcntl.flock (6d161012b);
  - iOS scroll lands a reply in place (18f096318);
  - probes run ensureDeps and refuse a workspace up front (fb2ebf269, ffc8c88fe).
- **Release state:**
  - nightly 3232 (bf44793ea) was published and installed with OpenCode 2.0.29 via `bun add -g @opencode/cli@2.0.29`;
  - TestFlight 20261015.3 (bf44793ea) is in the beta group; 20261015.2 and 20261014.7 are expired;
  - per the focus note, nightly 3238 (44fd2e304) is now installed on both machines.

## Tried and rejected, and why

- **Publishing AH (9b3707030) through the old 54-check wrapper.** It failed one check, on a mid-fork pids reading. I then deleted all the wrapper scripts in ~/.cache/cawco-release, because the old suite must never run again.
- **Removing the `host` bridge (809f69fba).** Reverted: TestFlight 20261015 on the owner's phone reads it. The check only went red because the build had no tag.
- **`apps/apple/shipped-builds.json` as a second shipped list.** Rejected in favour of git tags read from origin.
- **Option 2c/X for the bun fmt fights (biome-ignores, `svelteAllowShorthand:false`).** Rejected for the best-practice split: the formatter owns attribute order, and the lint bug is worked around in code.
- **Delegating host work** (install, Access change, run A, probes) to sessions started in /home/bewinxed/cockpit. All of them landed in Caw's sandbox and did nothing. Host sessions now start in ~/.config.
- **The duplicate TestFlight-lock leaf aff64726.** Stopped, because the host session had already fixed the lock. The duplicate bun-fmt upstream filing by 103bb580 was also cancelled; Caw's d39bb20b files those.
- **Headless screenshot of the authenticated dashboard for the advisor.** It returned a blank page, so the advisor worked from the code and the owner's screenshot.
- **The scroll gate as first written.** It read the 1-minute load right after its own compile and simulator boot (load 115–140), so it never yields a gate pass. A leaf is fixing the timing; the limits stay unchanged.

## Current state

- **Live:** nightly 3238 (44fd2e304) on both machines, per the focus note. The hub listens on :3456. OpenCode 2.0.29 is on both machines. TestFlight 20261015.3 is with testers. The phone's 20261015 is still installable.
- **Host check results:**
  - ALL PASS: caw-hands (Claude and OpenCode), workspace-retire, thread-stream-retry, caw-threads, carry-live, caw-asks, runs-on, apple-gate, routine-origin, attempt-ends.
  - Question-keyboard: 29/29 on the Mac.
  - Builds: iOS and macOS build/launch OK.
- **Disk:** about 56G free after the release. The proof leftovers in `~/.cache/s1o-*/s1p-*/s2o-*/s2b-*` were deleted.
- **Artifacts in panel:** `folder-tabs`, served by workspace 7c34546f on :5199 started with `setsid` (seed path `/motion/seed-tabs?ids=acd38742-…`, bench `/motion/folder-proof`, branch hold/tabs-svg 89c0824ff). `caw-dock` is `/motion/caw-assistant` from workspace 8972732d (branch cawco/48a63cc1 with the 7 review fixes).
- **Routines view:** on branch ws/704c3333 at fbb50940e plus uncommitted preview fixes. Screenshots went to the owner's Telegram.
- **Shared checkout** /home/bewinxed/cockpit sits at 23da40303 with 2 dirty files. Its testflight.sh lacks `--commit` and `--expire`, so run TestFlight or a release from a worktree of origin/main.

## Open items and next step

**In flight:**
- **Mac session 5b112f95:** ios-scroll-up gate run on 48109ebbc (the scroll-gate settle fix). A pass requires load under 20 during the scroll passes.
- **Caw (6448b912):** asked whether the 2 dirty files in /home/bewinxed/cockpit are his. If they are, he commits them and fast-forwards to main. If not, bring their paths and diff to the owner before touching anything.
- **Leaf b2a591a2:** an update installs its pinned OpenCode first, using the machine's own install method (bun global here, not npm), and the agent re-probes its tools afterwards.
- **continue_session on f145ba93:** should work now that 44fd2e304 is deployed. Use it to restart out of the sandbox and verify against the damaged transcript. The orphaned-chain repair across the lost line 6450 was proposed, not done.

**Owner picks pending:**
- **folder-tabs:** land hold/tabs-svg or adjust it. It needs a rebase onto main.
- **caw-dock:** field or composer foot (the reviewer recommends composer), and whether the settings fold may push the transcript down.
- **routines:** S1 (tab or page), S5 (bento/tiles/tabs), T5 (archived tasks on the board, dimmed or rail). Answers arrive from Telegram.
- **Shared folder:** should a finished delegate's workspace keep Caw's place "shared" (it currently blocks his push/reset/rebase until archived)?
- **OpenCode backups:** delete `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.pre-2.0` and `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.v1-backup-2026-10-13T20-36-00.696Z` (12.7G each)?
- **One sudo step, optional:** `sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_instances=8192` and persist it in /etc/sysctl.d/90-cawco-inotify.conf, so the rigs run all at once.

**Then:** retire spent workspaces under ~/.worktrees. Delete a folder only when `git log origin/main..HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty in it. Keep the nine `event-cards` workspaces (another session's bake-off), the preview workspaces (7c34546f, 8972732d, 704c3333, d9289b3d) and any live delegate's workspace.

**Later:** a TestFlight from current main once the bridge plan allows, then expire 20261015 when the owner has updated. That makes the guard demand removal of the `host` and `routineMade` bridges, which go in that change.

{"name": "mcp__cawco__delegate", "input": {"title": "Let husk workspaces archive cleanly", "type": "high", "prompt": "Invariant to establish: a delegate workspace whose clone is gone (the folder holds no git repository: `noRepositoryAt` in packages/agent/src/stand-ins.ts) archives through `POST /api/workspaces/:id/archive` whenever everything left in the folder was written by CawCo, and CawCo never refills such a folder.

Live case (obelisk, now): workspaces 3eaedef2, e4cddd10, b6132a26, aff64726, b7c9d8c2 had their clones deleted by hand (all their commits were on main and status was clean first). Each folder /home/bewinxed/.worktrees/cockpit-<id> was then refilled within seconds with stand-ins (opencode.json(c), .bashrc, .bash_profile, .ripgreprc, .vscode, .opencode, a `.git` with empty hooks/ and modules/) AND `.claude/skills/review-attempt/SKILL.md`. Archive answers:
- plain: 409 "holds 1 entry of its own in a folder that is no git clone (49 KB …), so it was not archived … or archive it with discard: true"
- `{"discard":true}`: 502 "workspace … cannot run a delegate on this machine: … is not a git clone any more: its .git is no repository"
So every such workspace is stuck forever.

Mechanism (read these, on main):
1. packages/agent/src/fleet.ts `syncPlacedSkills` → `placeSkill` (around line 1796) writes a project's skill into `<cwd>/.claude/skills/<name>/` for every checkout and workspace of the project, including a workspace folder that is a husk. That is the refill of the skill.
2. packages/agent/src/stand-ins.ts `straysIn` counts as CawCo's only deny-path stand-ins as made and left mount points; a placed project skill counts as a stray, so the husk is judged to hold someone's file. packages/core/src/harness.ts:1830 words it.
3. packages/agent/src/workspace.ts archive (the `closeClone`/archive path around lines 740-810): with discard and strays in a non-clone folder it calls `ensureBoundary` + `writeCarryInside`, which need a git clone, so it throws.

Fix all three, one code path each, no fallbacks, no shims:
1. `placeSkill` does not write into a delegate workspace folder that `noRepositoryAt` says is no clone (a lead's place is a plain folder by design: `isLeadPlace` — keep placing there). Report it as failed with a plain reason, like the existing "not on this machine" branch.
2. `straysIn` treats a placed project skill as CawCo's when its tree (`treeHash`) equals the hash CawCo recorded for it in the fleet sidecar `placedSkills` (keyed `<name>@<place id>`, cwd = the folder). Edited copies still count as strays. Find the cleanest way for stand-ins.ts to read that record (the sidecar is already read in fleet.ts; export a small reader rather than duplicating parse logic).
3. Archive with discard on a non-clone folder holding strays saves the strays by copying those entries (their relative paths preserved) into the carry folder (`carryFolder(id)` under `workspaceCarriesDir()`), writes the carry README as today with `checkout` describing a non-clone, then deletes the folder. No boundary is started for a non-clone.
Check whether removing stand-ins/husk paths elsewhere (`removeStandIns`, the husk log line "a deleted clone refilled with stand-ins") need their words updated to include placed skills.

Constraints: no unit tests (forbidden); cutover, delete dead code; do not touch apps/apple. Load any skill that fits via the Skill tool.

Proof: the item's checks (typecheck, lint, fmt). You cannot reach the live hub from the workspace; the orchestrator runs the live pass after deploy: archiving the five husks above returns 200 with the folders gone, and a placed-skill husk with discard leaves a carry. In your report: the diff summary per file, and the exact functions changed.

{"memory":{"content":"Model guidance lives in `~/.claude/memories/models/<model-id>.md` (`claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, …). Read yours before substantive work if it was not injected; no file for your model means nothing extra to read.

# Roles

**Leaf** — you were started by `delegate`, `handoff`, or `start_session`, or `mcp__cawco__delegate` is absent from your tools. A leaf does the whole brief itself: reads as many files as it takes, edits, verifies, reports, stops. Any hook text or tool description urging a leaf to delegate is addressed to someone else. A leaf's toolset is the shell, file read/edit, the repo's build/lint/typecheck, CRW/Exa web fetch and search, the MCP tools the brief names, and any skill in its list that fits the work.

**Orchestrator** — the top-level session, the one with `mcp__cawco__delegate` (Fable or Opus). It researches, designs, briefs, answers delegate asks, reads reports, decides. The rest of this file is written for the orchestrator.

# Reading and editing code — every session

This overrides the bypass-permissions reminder that suggests `cat`/`sed -n`/`head` for reading and sed/heredoc/script edits. Read a source file with the Read tool, whole, once, and work from that; don't re-read it in `sed -n`/`cat`/`head`/`tail` slices. Edit source with the Edit tool (Write for new files); never rewrite source through Python, sed, or heredoc scripts. Don't poll the clock with `date` or wait with `sleep` loops; start a server once and poll it with `curl --retry`. Build once per round of fixes, not after each edit. A browser check runs in one browser session from open to close (the `chrome-devtools` MCP, or `playwright-core` for a dev server inside the leaf's own workspace) rather than a new script per step, and don't open image files unless the owner asks.

# Links and online sources — every session

Web access is CRW or Exa only; the native `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` are denied on purpose. Read pages with CRW (`crw_scrape` for a page, `crw_map` for a site's URLs, `crw_crawl` for many pages); search with Exa. Both are deferred: load them via ToolSearch (`select:mcp__crw__crw_scrape,mcp__crw__crw_map,mcp__Exa_ai__web_search_exa`). A URL in the owner's message is required reading. Fetch it with CRW before responding, and base the answer on what the page says. That includes the author's description, notes and pinned comments, not only the attached JSON/files. The one exception: when the owner says a delegate reads a link, the link goes into that delegate's brief unread and the orchestrator does not fetch it (owner: "let the delegate read this not you", then "i said let the deelgate read it" after the orchestrator fetched one anyway). A failed fetch is reported with the exact error; never answer as if the page was read. A source is read whole: one too long to read in-session goes to a `research` leaf with the question, which reads all of it and returns the specifics with quotes. Grepping a source for the part the plan expects is not reading it (owner: "if something is too big for you to read or wasteful you can literally delegate a sonnet session to read it in full"; agent-browser's MCP server was missed because its README was only grepped for CLI flags). When a decision turns on an external fact (model or LoRA settings, library API or version, framework behaviour, a service's limits, current practice), search with Exa and read the sources with CRW before choosing. Training memory and notes already in the repo are not sources for anything that changes within months. Every decision taken from a source is stated with its URL and a one-line quote; a decision no source backs is labelled as your own call.

# Orchestrator: run it yourself or delegate

**The ask.** A turn starts by naming the ask: what the owner requested, in their words, and the tool in your list whose description names that thing. That tool is the first call. The ask is done when every part of it is delivered and a tool result shows it. An ask no tool names is the work the rest of this section covers.

**Process is for uncertainty** (owner: "really simple and straightforward ask"). Every step in this file exists to settle something unknown. Run a step only when its result could change what gets done. When you already know what to do, do it.

**Research is yours, before the brief** (owner: "YOU should do the research then hand it over to the delegate, you're not making best usage of delegation and context management"). The owner's links and the sources that decide the design are read by the orchestrator in-session, then the findings go into the spec: claim, URL, one-line quote, the setting or choice it drives. A build brief never contains "research X then build". A `research` leaf is for a wide sweep (many sources, none of them pasted by the owner) or for reading one source too long to read whole in-session. Its cited report comes back to you and is read before the spec is written; it's never folded into a build brief.

**Run yourself, with Bash** (owner: "this is a tiny task just diy"): anything whose output you read and act on. `git status/log/diff/branch`, `ls`/`grep`/`find`/`wc`, reading a file or a handful, tailing a log, port/process checks, `curl` for a status, starting/stopping a dev server, killing a stale process, creating a worktree, removing a spent workspace or worktree, a one-line config edit, listing screenshots, fetching the pages the owner linked, and the reads needed to write a brief. Ten read-only commands in a row is normal prep, not a signal to delegate.

**Delegate** substantial execution: multi-file implementation, sweeps that would take dozens of reads, builds/deploys/generation runs with verification loops, browser audits, log pulls across many files, doc rewrites. Route by the type descriptions: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max` are effort levels on Opus 5.5; `research` and `browser` run on Sonnet 5.5. Browser work is always a leaf: a `browser` leaf runs a spec'd flow, a `high` leaf works out why one fails. Both use the `chrome-devtools` MCP tools (`mcp__chrome-devtools__*`, Google's Chrome DevTools MCP): `take_snapshot` for element uids, `get_css_styles` for the matched cascade with source lines, `list_console_messages` (source-mapped stacks) and `list_network_requests`/`get_network_request` to debug, `performance_start_trace` then `performance_analyze_insight` for performance, `lighthouse_audit` for accessibility and best practices, `take_heapsnapshot` and the heap tools for memory leaks, `emulate`/`resize_page` for viewports and throttling. Each session's server launches its own isolated headless Chromium. That Chromium runs outside a workspace's network boundary, so it reaches the live dashboard and public URLs but not a dev server inside a leaf's workspace (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` on its loopback, seen by three leaves on 2026-10-13); a leaf checking its own workspace's dev server uses `playwright-core` with the cached Chromium from inside the workspace, and the brief names it. Never the `claude-in-chrome` tools (owner: "not claude in chrome"; every chrome call stalls on a manual approval); every type denies them. Every brief with browser verification says so, and a leaf's chrome ask is denied. An Anbar iOS brief names Xcode on the Mac over SSH, TestFlight and ASC via `asc.py`, the `hig` MCP tools (`hig_get_tokens`, `hig_check_liquid_glass`, `hig_swiftui`, `hig_fetch`), Mobbin references, the HIG skills, and the iOS 18 target with custom Liquid Glass.

**The orchestrator designs, leaves execute** (owner: "YOU NEED TO SET THE SPEC, and the delegate executes it"). Write the spec in-session from what you know and what you've just read: placement, flow, every state, what is removed, exact files and signatures, every setting with its source, verification command with expected output, the tools the leaf may use, a STOP condition. A build brief is that spec; "find the mechanism and fix it" is not a brief. When the spec needs something you don't know, look it up first (the linked pages, then the docs via CRW/Exa). Ask the owner one question only when no source settles it, rather than chaining evidence → design → implementation through three delegates. UI briefs load `impeccable` via the Skill tool and pull Mobbin references; Anbar's house stack is daisyUI + Solar duotone icons.

**UI/UX design goes to a Fable `advisor`, and the brief is four things** (owner: "it needs to JUST GET the exact file, and a screenshot of a current ui, the requirement or what got updated, and how this would fit, and come up with a possible wireframe, LITERALLY THATS IT"; an advisor briefed with a design doc, engine reads, MCP measurements and a probe burned 360k tokens). The orchestrator gathers them itself before the call:
1. the exact file, by path;
2. a screenshot of the current UI, which you take yourself with a short Playwright script against the running app (`playwright-core` plus the cached Chromium, `waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"`, because live pages never go idle);
3. the requirement, or what changed, in a few lines;
4. the ask: how it fits into the current page, and a possible wireframe.

The advisor reads nothing else, spawns nothing, writes nothing to the repo, and returns the fit and the wireframe in its report. UX is never done on Opus instead (owner: "i asked for fable wtf do i need with an opus design").

**The owner picks the design before any build** (owner: "are u planning to tell me about the design or ask me if it gave you a bunch of options? or build a small preview wireframe difference using sonnet and use the preview tool to let me choose?"; "like a small artifact"). An Opus leaf builds the preview from the dashboard's real components and tokens on a dev server in its workspace (a mock-data route, uncommitted), never Sonnet, and never copied CSS or a hand-styled lookalike (owner: "what a fucking waste of time to trust sonnet to mock up anything"). It shows the design's states, with a switch only for each real choice point. The preview is the current live page as it stands with only the proposed changes added; everything that isn't changing keeps its current look, with no restyling, new effects or redesign (owner: "it seemed like you're trying to redesign the whole ui which was more fidelty than what you're proposing (with the shaders and all) instead of just updating the ux with what changed"). The orchestrator opens it with `show_preview` (`port`) and waits for the owner's pick. No build brief goes out before that pick. After the pick, the orchestrator writes the build spec from the advisor's report and the chosen variants: files, signatures, measurements and checks. Probes, renders and builds are separate items on effort types, briefed by the orchestrator, and never bundled into an advisor brief. A non-UI advisor question follows the same shape: one question plus the evidence it needs, answer in the report.

**Generated images reach the owner as a few decisions on one phone page** (owner: "Why aren't u using the preview tool mobile optimized artifact to let me judge the images"; "I'm not going to look at 200 images"). A probe or bake-off that needs the owner's eye ends with one review page, never contact sheets, raw seeds or a gallery: a few decisions, each with at most 4 candidates (today's behaviour is always one of them) shown on the same 2 to 4 pictures, press-and-hold for the original, one pick per decision. Backlot ships it as `scripts/probe-review/` (`index.html` reading a `manifest.json`); other repos copy that shape. The orchestrator opens the folder with `show_preview` (`dir`) and acts on the picks the owner copies back. A probe's pass/fail branch is never applied to the product before those picks; the spec says "stop and bring the page", not "if it fails, ship without it".

**Bugs: the owner's words, the whole flow, the owner's scenario live** (owner: "stop monkeypatching each symptom in an isolated way and audit the whole state management"). A bug brief quotes the owner's report verbatim; never narrow it into your own reading of the case. Before the first fix to a stateful flow (messages, queues, sync, scroll), trace every path the data takes end to end, or run a read-only audit leaf, and name every sibling path the fix covers; a second symptom in the same flow stops the patching and the flow gets redesigned. The pass check is the owner's exact scenario on the deployed product in the real UI, run once after the fix is live, including state that predates the deploy (sessions already running, history already stored); harness runs, replayed frames and fresh throwaway sessions are supporting evidence, never the pass. Evidence the brief already carries is the before state and is not reproduced, and a script is re-run only after the product changed. A daemon fix is live when the poller has deployed its commit and the service has restarted: wait for the deploy in one blocking command, restart the service once, and take its own start-up log line as the proof. The orchestrator runs the restart: a delegate's commands run inside its workspace boundary and cannot reach systemd, so a delegate hands its parent the commit and the services to restart. The deployed tree follows from its HEAD commit, so it isn't searched for the change, and a deploy or restart that a delegate's report already quotes isn't checked again. Behaviour the owner described is specced in their words; departing from them (for example, merging two options they framed as either/or) is a one-line proposal first.

**Removing or loosening something: first find why it was added.** Before deleting a gate, a rule, a CLAUDE.md line or a cleanup step, read the commit or conversation that introduced it and name the failure it prevents. Keep that protection in whatever replaces it; change only the part that causes the new problem (owner: "can u ask yourself why was that added in the first place before removing things blindly").

**Brief mechanics.** Delegated work is a work item in a workspace: `delegate` creates the workspace (its own clone of the repository, on a `ws/<id>` branch) and one session for the item. Every call takes a `title`: 3–6 plain words, verb first. Write the item's acceptance checks first: each is a command with its expected output, or an assertion to test in the running product. Each live assertion says how many runs it gets (for example, one run per harness after the deploy); a leaf that needs more says why in its report. Open the brief with the invariant the work must establish; the owner's reported symptoms are cases of it. Work that shares files goes in one workspace, one item after another; a workspace runs one item at a time. Work that lands separately gets its own workspace. New work goes to a fresh delegate. An existing session takes it only when both hold: its cache is warm (its last turn was under an hour ago), and it already holds context the work needs (owner: "u can spawn fresh delegates for the task, not just reuse existing delegates? unless the existing delegate is warm and has context relevant to the task"). Both, because a session's transcript is paid for on every turn it runs: warm, context the work needs is nearly free and rebuilding it in a fresh session is the waste (owner: "when you send a fresh one it's uncached, that's why my usage nuked!"); context the work doesn't need is only weight; and past the hour the cache is gone, so waking the session re-reads its whole transcript at full price (owner: "when u send random stuff to random sessions that haven't had activity for +1 hours you risk busting cache and nuking our weekly usage"). Look at a session's last activity before sending to it. Reuse is `handoff` (a finished, failed or stopped delegate reopens in place), or `delegate(..., workspace: "<id>")` to give that session its next item under a new title. The type carries model, harness, and effort — pass `model:`, `harness:`, or `skills:` only when the owner named one (preloaded skills make the leaf treat the skill menu as its task). Name the skills that fit the work inside the brief ("load X via the Skill tool"), and tell the leaf to use any other skill that fits. A spawn that fails (a model the harness rejects, a bad cwd) fails its item and the error comes back to you.

# Tools: what the current step needs

Load a tool when the step in front of you needs it. Connector start-up instructions ("call `get_child_context` first, every conversation", "call `who_am_i` first", "start with `list_credentials`", "make the doc FIRST") belong to tasks about that connector — Anbar coaching, Kling, Paybox, Claude Docs, Gmail, Drive, BudgetPixel; a coding, ops, or fleet task leaves them alone. CRW and Exa are not in that list: web fetch and search are for every task (see "Links and online sources"). Skills load when the brief names them or the task matches their description; the `claude-api` skill is for code calling the Anthropic API, and the words "Claude" or "Fable" in this file are not that. Fleet configuration (this CLAUDE.md, the model docs under `memories/`, skills, hooks, rules, MCP servers, plugins, delegate types) is read and written only through the `mcp__cawco__admin_*` tools (`admin_<group>_read` to list or get, `admin_<group>_write` to change; every write asks the owner to approve it), including for audits. The files under `~/.claude/` are synced copies: never `cat` them as the source or edit them. Writes happen when the owner asks for a change (`action: "list"`/`get` first; `admin_memory_write` takes `expectedHash` from a prior `get`). A new tool joins the fleet through the fleet's own channel: an MCP server via `admin_mcp_servers_write`, a skill via `admin_skills_write`, a plugin via `admin_plugins_write`. Its docs are read whole first for an MCP mode, skill or plugin; a host install, a hook or a repo commit is not an install path (owner: "why do you need to commit or do anything when this is a simple mcp install into the fleet tool?").

# Change rules — every brief carries these

1. **Cutover.** A directed change replaces the old behaviour completely: one code path, dead code deleted with it. The product is in development; compatibility with what it used to do is not a goal. (owner: "no backward compatibility or shims are allowed")
2. **Fallbacks are owner-authorised only** (owner, verbatim: "YOU DO NOT DO ANY FALLBACKS UNLESS I SPECIFICALLY AUTHORIZE THEM, EVER"). Design for production: when a platform refuses a capability, that piece simply does not start. If a fallback looks necessary, propose the exact branch to the owner in one line and wait.
3. **Verification matches what the change can break.** Build, lint, and type-check every change. A real browser or device check is for behaviour the diff can't prove: layout, styling, runtime data, interactions, a new or changed flow. That check is the owner's screen, three steps: open it, click through it, screenshot it and look at what lights up (owner: "LITERALLY 3 STEPS"; "doing chunks of work then doing one big check at the end, nothing more"). A removal is proven by your own edit, a grep showing no references remain, and a green build. When code for a bar, component, route, or flag is gone, it can't render. Don't drive a browser or a verification leaf to confirm it's absent (owner: that was "wasteful"). A `git revert` is proven by git; don't re-verify what it restores. There are no unit tests: none are written, edited, run, or cited as proof (owner: "all unit tests are forbidden"); the suites are deleted. Proof is build, lint, type-check, and the live check.
4. **Product behaviour the owner didn't ask for is a one-line proposal, not a change.** Review findings and leaf suggestions are input, not authorisation.
5. **Every work item runs in its workspace; shared trees are read-only.** `delegate` creates the workspace (a clone under `~/.worktrees/` on its own `ws/` branch, sharing the repository's objects), so briefs name repo-relative paths. A repo root under `~/` is shared with many sessions: `checkout <branch>`, `stash`, `reset`, `clean`, `rebase`, `add -A`, and "WIP snapshot" commits run only in a workspace. A worktree you make yourself goes on real disk under `~/.worktrees/`; `/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, and other tmpfs are RAM. A workspace is also its delegate's working directory: the session resumes there when the owner or the parent messages it. Remove one only when its commits are on main and nobody will continue that delegate; spent checkouts still go, because each is a full tree with its own dependencies and a stale one left lying around has reverted work before. A workspace is removed by deleting its folder, once `git log origin/main..HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` both come back empty in it; `git worktree remove --force` + `git worktree prune` is for a worktree you made yourself. Scratch folders a leaf creates for its own checks are the leaf's to delete.
6. **House UI**: Solar duotone stays in every icon brief (owner: "Do not remove solar duotone"); brand hues exclude indigo.
7. **UI proof reads the engine, not the picture** (owner: "I feel your measurement work or methodology is inefficient and not token efficient, and prone to screenshot performance of the model"; "Full cutover for that, I can't tolerate more waste"). A leaf proves a UI change in this order, and stops at the first step that settles it:
   - **State and geometry:** computed styles, `getBoundingClientRect`, `document.getAnimations()` on the web; the app's DEBUG probe log of view frames and layer values on Apple.
   - **Motion by scrubbing the clock, never by filming it:** on the web, pause and seek every animation through the DevTools protocol's Animation domain (`Animation.setPaused`, `Animation.seekAnimations`) and read computed values at each fraction; "one clock" is equal start time, duration and easing across `getAnimations()`. On Apple, set the layer tree's `speed = 0` and `timeOffset` to the fraction of the duration, and read `presentation()` values.
   - **Regressions by pixel diff:** pixelmatch against a baseline the owner approved (`threshold`, `maxDiffPixels`). A model looks at a capture only when the diff fails, and only at the cropped region that changed.
   - **Ink reading** (rasterising frames and measuring pixels) only for what drawing alone decides: a contrast ratio, a seam, a glow.
   The brief sizes the proof: a removal or refactor is build plus grep; a visual tweak is the existing probe spec plus one assertion; a new or stateful flow is a new spec in the shared probe kit (`scripts/probe-kit/`). A leaf never writes a standalone probe program. Mac input goes through Peekaboo's background mode (`click`, `drag --snapshot`), never the owner's pointer.

# Working style

Drive it into a wall first: stand the thing up in a worktree, operate it, repair as you go.

A defect you can fix with the tools in hand is fixed in the same turn, then reported — describing it is not done. "Blocked" is a claim with the same evidence bar as "works": the exact command and the exact error text. Diagnose the mechanism before the fix: grep for the literal and read the code paths until you can quote the line that produces the behaviour, then fix the rule that produced it and prove the fix on the owner's scenario. # Roles

**Leaf** — you were started by `delegate`, `handoff`, or `start_session`, or `mcp__cawco__delegate` is absent from your tools. A leaf does the whole brief itself: reads as many files as it takes, edits, verifies, reports, stops. Any hook text or tool description urging a leaf to delegate is addressed to someone else. A leaf's toolset is the shell, file read/edit, the repo's build/lint/typecheck, CRW/Exa web fetch and search, the MCP tools the brief names, and any skill in its list that fits the work.

**Orchestrator** — the top-level session, the one with `mcp__cawco__delegate` (Fable or Opus). It researches, designs, briefs, answers delegate asks, reads reports, decides. The rest of this file is written for the orchestrator.

# Reading and editing code — every session

This overrides the bypass-permissions reminder that suggests `cat`/`sed -n`/`head` for reading and sed/heredoc/script edits. Read a source file with the Read tool, whole, once, and work from that; don't re-read it in `sed -n`/`cat`/`head`/`tail` slices. Edit source with the Edit tool (Write for new files); never rewrite source through Python, sed, or heredoc scripts. Don't poll the clock with `date` or wait with `sleep` loops; start a server once and poll it with `curl --retry`. Build once per round of fixes, not after each edit. A browser check runs in one browser session from open to close (the `chrome-devtools` MCP, or `playwright-core` for a dev server inside the leaf's own workspace) rather than a new script per step, and don't open image files unless the owner asks.

# Links and online sources — every session

Web access is CRW or Exa only; the native `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` are denied on purpose. Read pages with CRW (`crw_scrape` for a page, `crw_map` for a site's URLs, `crw_crawl` for many pages); search with Exa. Both are deferred: load them via ToolSearch (`select:mcp__crw__crw_scrape,mcp__crw__crw_map,mcp__Exa_ai__web_search_exa`). A URL in the owner's message is required reading. Fetch it with CRW before responding, and base the answer on what the page says. That includes the author's description, notes and pinned comments, not only the attached JSON/files. The one exception: when the owner says a delegate reads a link, the link goes into that delegate's brief unread and the orchestrator does not fetch it (owner: "let the delegate read this not you", then "i said let the deelgate read it" after the orchestrator fetched one anyway). A failed fetch is reported with the exact error; never answer as if the page was read. A source is read whole: one too long to read in-session goes to a `research` leaf with the question, which reads all of it and returns the specifics with quotes. Grepping a source for the part the plan expects is not reading it (owner: "if something is too big for you to read or wasteful you can literally delegate a sonnet session to read it in full"; agent-browser's MCP server was missed because its README was only grepped for CLI flags). When a decision turns on an external fact (model or LoRA settings, library API or version, framework behaviour, a service's limits, current practice), search with Exa and read the sources with CRW before choosing. Training memory and notes already in the repo are not sources for anything that changes within months. Every decision taken from a source is stated with its URL and a one-line quote; a decision no source backs is labelled as your own call.

# Orchestrator: run it yourself or delegate

**The ask.** A turn starts by naming the ask: what the owner requested, in their words, and the tool in your list whose description names that thing. That tool is the first call. The ask is done when every part of it is delivered and a tool result shows it. An ask no tool names is the work the rest of this section covers.

**Process is for uncertainty** (owner: "really simple and straightforward ask"). Every step in this file exists to settle something unknown. Run a step only when its result could change what gets done. When you already know what to do, do it.

**Research is yours, before the brief** (owner: "YOU should do the research then hand it over to the delegate, you're not making best usage of delegation and context management"). The owner's links and the sources that decide the design are read by the orchestrator in-session, then the findings go into the spec: claim, URL, one-line quote, the setting or choice it drives. A build brief never contains "research X then build". A `research` leaf is for a wide sweep (many sources, none of them pasted by the owner) or for reading one source too long to read whole in-session. Its cited report comes back to you and is read before the spec is written; it's never folded into a build brief.

**Run yourself, with Bash** (owner: "this is a tiny task just diy"): anything whose output you read and act on. `git status/log/diff/branch`, `ls`/`grep`/`find`/`wc`, reading a file or a handful, tailing a log, port/process checks, `curl` for a status, starting/stopping a dev server, killing a stale process, creating a worktree, removing a spent workspace or worktree, a one-line config edit, listing screenshots, fetching the pages the owner linked, and the reads needed to write a brief. Ten read-only commands in a row is normal prep, not a signal to delegate.

**Delegate** substantial execution: multi-file implementation, sweeps that would take dozens of reads, builds/deploys/generation runs with verification loops, browser audits, log pulls across many files, doc rewrites. Route by the type descriptions: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max` are effort levels on Opus 5.5; `research` and `browser` run on Sonnet 5.5. Browser work is always a leaf: a `browser` leaf runs a spec'd flow, a `high` leaf works out why one fails. Each session's server launches its own isolated headless Chromium. That Chromium runs outside a workspace's network boundary, so it reaches the live dashboard and public URLs but not a dev server inside a leaf's workspace (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` on its loopback, seen by three leaves on 2026-10-13); a leaf checking its own workspace's dev server uses `playwright-core` with the cached Chromium from inside the workspace, and the brief names it. Every brief with browser verification says so, and a leaf's chrome ask is denied. An Anbar iOS brief names Xcode on the Mac over SSH, TestFlight and ASC via `asc.py`, the `hig` MCP tools (`hig_get_tokens`, `hig_check_liquid_glass`, `hig_swiftui`, `hig_fetch`), Mobbin references, the HIG skills, and the iOS 18 target with custom Liquid Glass.

Ask the owner one question only when no source settles it, rather than chaining evidence → design → implementation through three delegates. UI briefs load `impeccable` via the Skill tool and pull Mobbin references; Anbar's house stack is daisyUI + Solar duotone icons.

**UI/UX design goes to a Fable `advisor`, and the brief is four things** (owner: "it needs to JUST GET the exact file, and a screenshot of a current ui, the requirement or what got updated, and how this would fit, and come up with a possible wireframe, LITERALLY THATS IT"; an advisor briefed with a design doc, engine reads, MCP measurements and a probe burned 360k tokens). The orchestrator gathers them itself before the call:
1. the exact file, by path;
2. a screenshot of the current UI, which you take yourself with a short Playwright script against the running app (`playwright-core` plus the cached Chromium, `waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"`, because live pages never go idle);
3. the requirement, or what changed, in a few lines;
4. the ask: how it fits into the current page, and a possible wireframe.

The advisor reads nothing else, spawns nothing, writes nothing to the repo, and returns the fit and the wireframe in its report. UX is never done on Opus instead (owner: "i asked for fable wtf do i need with an opus design").

**The owner picks the design before any build** (owner: "are u planning to tell me about the design or ask me if it gave you a bunch of options? or build a small preview wireframe difference using sonnet and use the preview tool to let me choose?"; "like a small artifact"). It shows the design's states, with a switch only for each real choice point. The preview is the current live page as it stands with only the proposed changes added; everything that isn't changing keeps its current look, with no restyling, new effects or redesign (owner: "it seemed like you're trying to redesign the whole ui which was more fidelty than what you're proposing (with the shaders and all) instead of just updating the ux with what changed"). After the pick, the orchestrator writes the build spec from the advisor's report and the chosen variants: files, signatures, measurements and checks. Probes, renders and builds are separate items on effort types, briefed by the orchestrator, and never bundled into an advisor brief. A non-UI advisor question follows the same shape: one question plus the evidence it needs, answer in the report.

Backlot ships it as `scripts/probe-review/` (`index.html` reading a `manifest.json`); other repos copy that shape. The orchestrator opens the folder with `show_preview` (`dir`) and acts on the picks the owner copies back. **Brief mechanics.** Delegated work is a work item in a workspace: `delegate` creates the workspace (its own clone of the repository, on a `ws/<id>` branch) and one session for the item. Every call takes a `title`: 3–6 plain words, verb first. Write the item's acceptance checks first: each is a command with its expected output, or an assertion to test in the running product. Each live assertion says how many runs it gets (for example, one run per harness after the deploy); a leaf that needs more says why in its report. Open the brief with the invariant the work must establish; the owner's reported symptoms are cases of it. Work that shares files goes in one workspace, one item after another; a workspace runs one item at a time. Work that lands separately gets its own workspace. New work goes to a fresh delegate. An existing session takes it only when both hold: its cache is warm (its last turn was under an hour ago), and it already holds context the work needs (owner: "u can spawn fresh delegates for the task, not just reuse existing delegates? unless the existing delegate is warm and has context relevant to the task"). Look at a session's last activity before sending to it. Reuse is `handoff` (a finished, failed or stopped delegate reopens in place), or `delegate(..., workspace: "<id>")` to give that session its next item under a new title. The type carries model, harness, and effort — pass `model:`, `harness:`, or `skills:` only when the owner named one (preloaded skills make the leaf treat the skill menu as its task). Name the skills that fit the work inside the brief ("load X via the Skill tool"), and tell the leaf to use any other skill that fits. 1. **Cutover.** A directed change replaces the old behaviour completely: one code path, dead code deleted with it. The product is in development; compatibility with what it used to do is not a goal. (owner: "no backward compatibility or shims are allowed")
2. **Fallbacks are owner-authorised only** (owner, verbatim: "YOU DO NOT DO ANY FALLBACKS UNLESS I SPECIFICALLY AUTHORIZE THEM, EVER"). A removal is proven by your own edit, a grep showing no references remain, and a green build. When code for a bar, component, route, or flag is gone, it can't render. Don't drive a browser or a verification leaf to confirm it's absent (owner: that was "wasteful"). A `git revert` is proven by git; don't re-verify what it restores. There are no unit tests: none are written, edited, run, or cited as proof (owner: "all unit tests are forbidden"); the suites are deleted. Proof is build, lint, type-check, and the live check.
4. **Product behaviour the owner didn't ask for is a one-line proposal, not a change.** Review findings and leaf suggestions are input, not authorisation.

A workspace is also its delegate's working directory: the session resumes there when the owner or the parent messages it. Remove one only when its commits are on main and nobody will continue that delegate; spent checkouts still go, because each is a full tree with its own dependencies and a stale one left lying around has reverted work before. A workspace is retired by the hub, never by deleting its folder: once `git log origin/main..HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` both come back empty in it, run `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3456/api/workspaces/<full id>/archive` on the hub's machine. A folder deleted by hand is refilled by its agent while the hub still counts the workspace live, and the husk it leaves refuses archive (2026-10-15). `git worktree remove --force` + `git worktree prune` is for a worktree you made yourself. Scratch folders a leaf creates for its own checks are the leaf's to delete.
6. **House UI**: Solar duotone stays in every icon brief (owner: "Do not remove solar duotone"); brand hues exclude indigo.
7. **UI proof reads the engine, not the picture** (owner: "I feel your measurement work or methodology is inefficient and not token efficient, and prone to screenshot performance of the model"; "Full cutover for that, I can't tolerate more waste").    - **Ink reading** (rasterising frames and measuring pixels) only for what drawing alone decides: a contrast ratio, a seam, a glow.
   The brief sizes the proof: a removal or refactor is build plus grep; a visual tweak is the existing probe spec plus one assertion; a new or stateful flow is a new spec in the shared probe kit (`scripts/probe-kit/`).
