Title: FAQ: Can I paste CSS in Penpot Inspect to create design?
URL: https://community.penpot.app/t/faq-can-i-paste-css-in-penpot-inspect-to-create-design/2576
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
The short answer is “not yet”. But the long answer needs a bit of context.
...
Penpot supports various CSS generation options tied to our Layout features. Since we use open standards (SVG/HTML/CSS) to render our design, it’s trivial for us to give you an exact CSS representation of the layout rules that apply to your design as well as any SVG code that you require.
...
We now support CSS Grid on top of CSS Flex, and other CSS rendering methods will follow.

Going from a design artifact to its CSS representation is simple enough because you control the means of which that design artifact (ie: a board with multiple elements arranged in a particular way) is created. The design activity uses discrete Penpot options to produce a valid result, like padding input or alignment choices.

The other way round is tougher, though. Getting ANY CSS code and inferring a no-loss deterministic design representation would require processing the input and pushing it through a CSS rendering engine, like browsers have. We would need to work on a 1:1 representation between any CSS property and Penpot visual representation.
...
Pasting code into Penpot is definitely something that would be supercool, but we need to understand the main use case for this. If the use case is “I prefer to directly edit CSS code for Flex Layout input rather than using Penpot UI” then we don’t see a very compelling use case given the complexity of the task.
...
I could see a situation where a developer would paste the framework on a page into penpot to allow designer to then build on top of that.
...
Btw. on professional level in modern era of interface design, we don’t need everything generated by design tools. We (both designers and developers) need to understand more about how it works on both sides. Building (also both design and development) interfaces for decade, and I never use everything from generated code in Adobe XD, Sketch, Figma etc. Since this is really nice that you can copy and paste the whole code from design tools and it works, I think it’s not so much useful in most of the cases, because we use preselected variables, we have own system, we know how to define CSS and so on (I mean if you do it for a living).

Having something like code inspector, where I can see separated predefined styles like colors, typography, spacing, border radiuses, etc. is something where I see huge value. If design tool allow me define styles or layout properties like spacing (that are used across the design files), and then export e.g. in various formats (CSS, Sass, JSON etc.), then it starts to get quite interesting and no design tool has it yet. This transfers more responsibility to the designer, and the developer cannot then implement the designs incorrectly, because he simply has everything he needs.
...
Existing Design Systems, that run on SASS, LESS, or CSS could be incorporated into a library feature. The “Single Source of Truth”, for any Design System should live in the codebase/repo/NPM package itself, not in a design tool. Human error is introduced when a Dev tries to copy and paste hundreds of code snippets into their own SASS/LESS/CSS within the application codebase, and this removes governance.

On the other hand, if a CSS resource can be imported, and the Classes used within the GUI, this limits human error. Versioning becomes much easier as well, and would be comparable to an NPM package update that just “works”. If resource handoff is a priority for any enterprise team, this feature would be critical.

The Use Case I envision is this… I draw a square. Turn it into a component. Select a CSS “library” within s dropdown, and then apply classes to that portion of the component.
Eg. Class Field: [abc-btn abc-btn—primary]

The imported CSS styles the button in the Penpot interface, and matches what a Dev already has installed via NPM.
...
My use case for that is while using an AI tool to help me design. I want to get code (CSS/HTML) from an AI tool, import it in Penpot, and then be open to modify it graphicaly by my will or by code with suggestions from AI.

6. **Self-hosting is a real server stack.**
   - Docker Compose with several services: frontend, backend, exporter, Postgres, Valkey, and since 2.18 an admin console.
   - It needs "some technical knowledge: Docker and Docker Compose, basic DNS management, and proxy configuration", and HTTPS ("the clipboard does not work with HTTP").

**The rule** (agent tree-swap.ts, shared by skills and plugins)
- `placeTree` now writes the tree's `.cawco-carried.json` itself, listing the files the fleet sent. A file the fleet tries to send under that name is refused.
- `heldHash(path, known?)` hashes exactly those files in the hub's `hashFiles`. A carried file that changed reads as a change. A missing one counts as missing, never as equal to the fleet's copy. Any other file in the folder is ignored.
- `skillDrift` itself is unchanged. It now compares these hashes, so editing SKILL.md or a carried script still freezes the skill, as before.
- **Carry-over:** the new tree takes every file of the current one that is in neither the old nor the new carried list (`__pycache__`, notes). Files the last version carried and this one drops are still removed. Anything that would collide with a new file or its folder is skipped.

**Skills written before trees kept a list** (that state predates the deploy)
- When the sync carries the skill's files, the tree is judged over the fleet's current file list, then written once more so it gets its own list (`holdsFleetCopy`).
- Otherwise it is judged over its whole folder, today's rule. So an edit made before this change still freezes the skill and is not overwritten.

**Where the rule now applies**
- `heldSkills` (now takes the sync's payload) and `syncSkillFiles`, for Claude Code and, through fleet-common, OpenCode and pi.

Headline: Safari now finds the edge strips: in the probe's replay of WebKit's edge lookup, the top edge is the dimmed bar with the drawer open and the bar itself on the home, in light and dark. The spec passes 152 of 152 (88 fail against the old component); typecheck and lint pass.

## Cause
- **How Safari picks the colour:** WebKit finds the colour it extends past each edge in `LocalFrameView.cpp` `fixedContainerEdges` (the source joshpuckett.me/seamless-mobile-safari links: "how Safari's sampling works").
  - It hit-tests the middle of each viewport edge (`midpointOnSide`: top at `rect.y()`, bottom at `rect.maxY()`), ignoring CSS pointer-events.
  - It walks up the hit renderer's lineage to the first fixed or sticky box (`findFixedContainer`) and takes that box's own background colour.
  - With none, it falls back to the page background.
- **Why the strips were missed:** they were `::after` pseudo-elements on static `.edge-top`/`.edge-bottom` hosts. A pseudo hits as its host, so the walk went div → body → html, found no fixed box, and fell back to the page background, which is body's bottom colour.
- **This matches every Simulator reading:**
  - light home top (247,244,238) is the light page ground;
  - dark home top (29,27,24) is the dark page ground;
  - dark drawer top (35,33,30) is the drawer's surface, which this change sets as body's colour while the drawer is open;
  - the sidebar passed only because body equals the sidebar's ground there.

## Fix (`apps/dashboard/src/lib/cawco/ScreenEdges.svelte`)
- `.edge-top` and `.edge-bottom` are now the fixed, painted boxes themselves (same geometry: 12px or the safe area, 7px past the edge, z 1001, `pointer-events: none`, opacity and transitions as before). There is no `::after`.
- `theme-color` is read from the element's own background. It is also re-read when `theme.resolved` changes, because `:root.theme-flip *` turns transitions off on elements during a theme flip (it skipped pseudo-elements before).

## Spec (`scripts/probe-kit/specs/web/safari-edges.ts`)
- **New check, Safari's pick:** a replay of WebKit's lookup. Force pointer-events on, take `elementFromPoint` at (mid, 0) and (mid, innerHeight − 1), and walk up to the first visible fixed or sticky ancestor. Assert it is `div.edge-top`/`div.edge-bottom` and that its colour equals the composited surface painted under that edge.
- **Composited comparisons:** html, body and `theme-color` are now compared against the composited top and bottom surfaces rather than the strip.
- **Results:**
  - **new component:** 152 PASS, ALL PASS (WebKit build 2359 via `PROBE_WEBKIT`), including:
    - dark bottom sheet: `div.edge-top` (24,22,20) vs (23,22,20);
    - light home: `div.edge-top` (254,253,250) vs (254,253,250);
    - light bottom sheet: (248,246,241) vs (249,246,242);
    - dark home: (35,33,30).
  - **old component, same spec:** 88 FAILED. The pick landed on `div.toast-layer` (transparent), e.g. "light home: … (div.toast-layer rgba(0,0,0,0) vs rgba(254,253,250,255))".
- `bun run typecheck`: 23 checks passed. `bun run lint:changed`: exit 0 (css-scope clean).

## The "Connecting…" at :3000
It isn't the origin gate. `:3000` is a `vite dev` server, and its `/ws` relay (vite.config.ts `server.proxy`, `gateHubSocket`) admits a direct-IP page, since `Origin` equals `publicOrigin()` built from `Host`. It forwards only to the `CAWCO_DEV_HUB_URL` that dev server was started with, so "Connecting…" means that hub didn't answer. The hub's own `/ws/dashboard` has no origin gate.

## Simulator re-check after this lands
Run the same steps as before; the two failing rows should now read:
- dark New-session drawer: top band (24,22,20), the dimmed bar;
- light home: top band (254,253,250), the bar.

Use the production dashboard address, not the `:3000` dev server.

# Designs and live components (D29, merged) — the spec

Sources: PRD §5.7, §5.10, decision log; the brief's evidence (pen.dev, Paper, Onlook, Svelte 5's `__svelte_meta`, code-inspector, Vite). Own-knowledge claims are marked "(own knowledge; probe N)". Nothing beyond the PRD read; nothing written.

## 0. The invariant and the answer

**A component exists exactly once. Everything on the canvas is an instance of it.** Nothing is re-coded per variant, per screen, per import, or per render.

A **design** is an artifact: a tree of artboards, frames, text, images, icons, instances, slots and notes, laid out with a small flex vocabulary and coloured, sized and typeset by the project's token names. Every `instance` points at one component. A component is one record in the project's library with a name, typed props (enums are the variants), named slots, and **one body**: either a **design body** (a tree in CawCo's neutral medium, for a project before it has code) or a **code body** (the real file in the project, for a project with code). The canvas, the pins, the tools and the person's editing see only the contract (name, props, slots, ids); which body a component has decides only *who draws it*: CawCo's renderer expands a design body; the project's own toolchain, run by the daemon inside the workspace, mounts a code body with the instance's props. When a project writes code for a design-backed component, that is a one-time port of the body; the record switches to `code=`, the tree body is deleted, and the instances do not change. Existing code is never recreated on the canvas: the file is the component, and the library record for it is a signature, not a copy.

## 1. The document: one tree, written as markup

Decision from the second spec, unchanged: a node tree stored in the artifact's Yjs doc (`nodes`), serialised for agents and for files as HTML-shaped markup with stable node ids, rendered by CawCo to HTML/CSS. Why: agents write HTML-shaped markup best and patch by id precisely (pen's MCP shape); a fixed flex vocabulary draws the same in every WebKit and Blink web view (own knowledge; probe 1); every node type has a direct SwiftUI, Flutter, React Native and web form, which raw HTML/CSS does not; OpenUI Lang is an app-view language with queries and tools, not a design document.

Node types: `design` (root; `tokens=` names the token CSS), `artboard` (device preset phone|tablet|desktop|free, width), `frame` (`layout` row|column|free, `gap`, `pad`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `width`/`height` fixed|hug|fill, `fill`, `stroke`, `radius`, `shadow`, `clip`, `scroll`, `hidden`), `text` (`style`, `color`, `align`, `lines`, content), `image` (`asset`, `fit`), `icon` (set name; CawCo's own is Solar duotone), `instance` (`of`, prop values, children fill the default slot, `slot=` names another), `slot` (a named hole inside a design body), `override` (design-backed only, §2), `note` (annotation, never ported). `choice`/`option` on any node for picks (D19). 1	A feasibility spike. It answers six questions with measurements and builds no product. Nothing lands; the report at docs/spikes/component-stage.md is the deliverable.
2	
3	The owner chose this design ("Ok do C"), in his words across the conversation:
4	- "Are you not able to dynamically create and render svelte components in the preview?"
5	- "something how pen or paper does it"
6	- "are you unable to have reusable components without having the agent rewrite it which leads to the defects this whole thing was made to prevent"
7	- "this needs to work for all our users, across their many languages and frameworks"
8	
9	The design (option C):
10	- A component exists once: the project's real file.
11	- An agent composes instances of real components with mock props and variants side by side in a **stage file** written in the project's own language (e.g. `cards.stage.svelte`, importing `$lib/cawco/transcript/*.svelte` and the app's global CSS). Variants are marked with `data-cawco-variant="<id>"`; picks use `data-cawco-choice`/`data-option`.
12	- CawCo's daemon runs the project's own Vite programmatically from the workspace's own node_modules, with a small CawCo Vite plugin added, and shows the stage through the hub's preview proxy.
13	- A click maps to `file:line:column`: Svelte via `__svelte_meta`, other frameworks via a vendored code-inspector transform.
14	- Nothing is re-coded.
15	
16	Answer each question with the exact commands, numbers and the lines that decided it:
17

1 # Live components: prior art for rendering and editing real Svelte 5 components 2 3 Research only, no code changes. Date: 2026-10-16. 4 5 **Scope (widened by the owner):** "this needs to work for all our users, across their many languages and frameworks". Sections 1–5 were first answered for Svelte, the framework the questions named. Each now carries a **Cross-framework** note, and sections 6–8 add code-inspector, Storybook CSF as a cross-framework standard, and non-web stacks. 6 7 **The one-paragraph answer.** 8 9 - **Source mapping.** Every framework-agnostic tool stamps a `file:line:col` string onto elements at compile or transform time, then reads it back from the DOM. 10 - code-inspector does this for 7 web frameworks and 7 bundlers. 11 - Onlook does it for JSX only. 12 - Svelte stamps it natively, in dev builds, as `__svelte_meta`. 13 - **Rendering.** Nothing renders arbitrary frameworks without running the user's own dev command. 14 - Onlook's current desktop app runs the project's dev server and shows it in frames. 15 - Storybook needs a per-framework renderer plus a builder. 16 - **Native stacks.** Native stacks (SwiftUI, Flutter, Compose, React Native) have no DOM to map. Their tools are IDE-bound, or are code generators rather than editors. 17 18 **How I read the sources.** The shell could reach GitHub, so I shallow-cloned the repos and read the files directly. File paths below are repo-relative to the clone. Commits read: 19 20 - onlook `423e2e9` 21 - addon-svelte-csf `f2b2329`, v5.1.5 22 - poveste `47f4232`, v0.19.1 23 - svelte.dev `89f941c`, `@sveltejs/repl` 0.6.0 24 - Glide, cloned HEAD 25 26 **Read whole** means I read the file top to bottom. **Skimmed** means a grep, an Exa search highlight, or a README. Anything unread is listed in the coverage table at the end. 27 28 --- 29 30 ## 1. Onlook (github.com/onlook-dev/onlook) 31 32 **Licence.** Apache-2.0. `LICENSE.md` opens "Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004", and the root `package.json` has `"license": "Apache-2.0"`. 33 34 ### 1a. Canvas element → source 35 36 - **The attribute is `data-oid`.** `packages/constants/src/editor.ts` has `DATA_ONLOOK_ID = 'data-oid'`. It is written into the user's source file, not injected at render time. 37 - **Where it is injected.** `packages/parser/src/ids.ts` `addOidsToAst` walks every `JSXOpeningElement` and pushes `t.jSXAttribute(t.jSXIdentifier('data-oid'), t.stringLiteral(oid))`. Fragments are skipped. Duplicates are replaced. 38 - **When it runs.** `packages/file-system/src/code-fs.ts` `processJsxFile()` runs on every file write: parse → `addOidsToAst(ast, existingOids)` → regenerate → `formatContent`. The oid therefore persists in the repo and survives HMR. 39 - **The index.** `updateMetadataForFile()` calls `createTemplateNodeMap` (`packages/parser/src/template-node/map.ts`) and stores `index[oid] = {path, startTag{line,column}, endTag, component, dynamicType, coreElementType}`. 40 - `component` comes from a `componentStack` of enclosing function, class and variable names. 41 - `dynamicType` flags array `.map` roots and conditional roots. 42 - **Browser side.** `apps/web/preload/script/helpers/ids.ts` reads it back with `getOid(node) { return node.getAttribute(EditorAttributes.DATA_ONLOOK_ID) }`. 43 - The preload script also assigns a runtime `data-odid` (`odid-${nanoid()}`) per DOM node. 44 - **Instances.** Components get a second pair, `data-oiid` (instance id) and `data-ocname` (component name). 45 - `apps/web/preload/script/api/elements/index.ts` `updateElementInstance` sets both with `el.setAttribute(...)`. 46 - `apps/web/client/src/components/store/editor/ast/index.ts` `findNodeInstance` computes them by walking up the layer tree and matching the parent's metadata. 47 - Insert targeting uses `targetOid: getInstanceId(parent) || getOid(parent)` (`preload/script/api/elements/helpers.ts:84`). 48 - Style edits switch target with `oid: this.mode === StyleMode.Instance ? selectedEl.instanceId : selectedEl.oid` (`store/editor/style/index.ts:135`). So "edit this instance" means "edit the call site". 49 50 ### 1b. Canvas edit → code change 51 52 The pipeline is in `apps/web/client/src/components/store/editor/code/requests.ts`: 53 54 1. Each editor action (`UpdateStyleAction`, `InsertElementAction`, `EditTextAction`, `MoveElementAction`, …) becomes a `CodeDiffRequest` keyed by oid. 55 2. Requests are grouped per file into `FileToRequests`. 56 3. `processGroupedRequests`: `getAstFromContent(content)` → `transformAst(ast, oidToRequest)` → `getContentFromAst(ast, content)`. It returns `{original, generated, path}` diffs. 57 58 Parser and printer: 59 60 - **Library:** Babel via `@babel/standalone`. `packages/parser/src/packages.ts` has `export const { parse } = packages.parser; generate = packages.generator; traverse = packages.traverse.default`. 61 - **Parse options** (`parse.ts`): `sourceType: 'module'`, plugins `typescript`, `jsx`, decorators, etc. 62 - **Printing** (`parse.ts` `getContentFromAst`): `generate(ast, {retainLines: true, comments: true, retainFunctionParens: true, …}, originalContent)`. 63 - **Formatting:** `packages/parser/src/prettier/index.ts` runs `prettier/standalone` with the TypeScript and ESTree plugins. ` children. | 72 | Insert | `insert.ts` | Appends, prepends or inserts at an index in the target's `children`. The element comes from `getAstFromCodeblock(codeBlock, stripIds=true)` or is built from `{tagName, attributes, children}`. | 73 | Move | `move.ts` | Finds the child by oid, adds a `key` and splices it to the new index. | 74 | Remove, group, ungroup, insert-image | `remove.ts`, `group.ts`, `image.ts` | Not read. | 75 76 ### 1c. Composition 77 78 An inserted component is a JSX code block text (`CodeInsert.codeBlock`) parsed into an AST node, given an oid via `addParamToElement`, and spliced into the parent's `children` at `append`, `prepend` or `index`. There is no separate component-instance model. 79 80 Reorder is `CodeMove{oid, location.index}`. 81 82 Props are limited to what `updateNodeProp` can express: strings, booleans, empty functions and identifiers. Props with complex expressions are not modelled. 83 84 ### 1d. Reuse for Svelte 85 86 **Framework-neutral concepts (reuse as design):** 87 88 - the stable-id → `{path, start/end line/col, component}` index 89 - the action set: style, text, move, insert, remove, group 90 - grouping requests per file and producing `{original, generated}` diffs for review 91 - the instance-vs-definition edit mode (`oiid` vs `oid`) 92 93 **React/Babel-bound code (not reusable as code):** 94 95 - everything under `packages/parser/src/code-edit/*` and `template-node/*` operates on `JSXElement`, `JSXAttribute`, `JSXText` 96 - `getTemplateNodeChild` matches `(node.openingElement.name as JSXIdentifier).name === child.component` 97 - `isReactFragment`, `.map` array-root detection and the Next.js `injectPreloadScript` are React or Next specific 98 99 **Svelte substitution.** Svelte's `__svelte_meta.loc` replaces the `data-oid` injection. 100 101 - `sveltejs/svelte` `packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dev/elements.js` sets `element.__svelte_meta = {parent: dev_stack, loc: {file: filename, line: location[0], column: location[1]}}`. 102 - The inspector adds 1 to both (`file_loc = ${file}:${line + 1}:${column + 1}`), so they are 0-based. This is from the Exa-fetched `Inspector.svelte` highlight, skimmed. 103 - The loc is a dev-compile value. No file is modified. The cost is that there is no persistent id: a loc goes stale after any edit and must be re-read from the DOM, or the file re-parsed, after each write. 104 - For writes, Svelte has no Babel-equivalent that keeps formatting. 105 - addon-svelte-csf's `src/compiler/plugins.ts` says: "Printing the AST again collapses the whitespace between nodes". 106 - The practical Svelte path is `svelte/compiler` `parse(..., {modern:true})` for node offsets plus `magic-string` splices. 107 - Glide's `packages/adapters/svelte/src/index.ts` takes a cruder route: regex over the tag text, found by `data-gl-source` or a `findTagAtLineCol` helper. 108 109 **Cross-framework.** 110 111 - **Claimed reach.** The Onlook README (`onlook-dev/onlook`, "How it works") says: "This architecture can theoretically scale to any language or framework that displays DOM elements declaratively (e.g. jsx/tsx/html). We are focused on making it work well with Next.js and TailwindCSS for now." 112 - That is a statement of intent. The code only handles JSX. 113 - **Per-framework cost.** The id-injection and edit passes are the part that must be rewritten per framework: a template parser plus a splice. 114 - code-inspector shows the injection half is already solved for Vue, Svelte, Astro, MDX and Pug with one transform per language (section 6). 115 - Nobody has an open-source *edit* half beyond JSX (Onlook) and CSS blocks (stylewright). 116 117 --- 118 119 ## 2. Storybook Svelte CSF (github.com/storybookjs/addon-svelte-csf) 120 121 **Licence.** MIT (`LICENSE`: "MIT License … Copyright (c) 2021 Storybook contributors"; `package.json` `"license": "MIT"`). 122 123 **Versions and peers.** v5.1.5. `peerDependencies`: `svelte ^5.0.0`, `vite ^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8`, `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte ^4..^7`, `storybook` and `@storybook/svelte`. 124 125 ### 2a. How `.stories.svelte` is parsed and compiled 126 127 There are three stages, all keyed to the regex `/\.stories\.svelte$/`: 128 129 1. **Indexer** (`src/indexer/index.ts` + `parser.ts`). 130 - `parseForIndexer(filename)` parses with `svelte/compiler` and returns `{meta, stories, isLegacy}`: title, tags, and each ``'s `exportName` and `name`. 131 - It needs only `svelte/compiler`, plus `loadSvelteConfig` from vite-plugin-svelte and `fs`. 1	# Designs and live components (D29, merged) — the spec
2	
3	Sources: PRD §5.7, §5.10, decision log; the brief's evidence (pen.dev, Paper, Onlook, Svelte 5's `__svelte_meta`, code-inspector, Vite). Own-knowledge claims are marked "(own knowledge; probe N)". Nothing beyond the PRD read; nothing written.
4	
5	## 0. The invariant and the answer
6	
7	**A component exists exactly once. Everything on the canvas is an instance of it.** Nothing is re-coded per variant, per screen, per import, or per render.
8	
9	A **design** is an artifact: a tree of artboards, frames, text, images, icons, instances, slots and notes, laid out with a small flex vocabulary and coloured, sized and typeset by the project's token names. Every `instance` points at one component. A component is one record in the project's library with a name, typed props (enums are the variants), named slots, and **one body**: either a **design body** (a tree in CawCo's neutral medium, for a project before it has code) or a **code body** (the real file in the project, for a project with code). The canvas, the pins, the tools and the person's editing see only the contract (name, props, slots, ids); which body a component has decides only *who draws it*: CawCo's renderer expands a design body; the project's own toolchain, run by the daemon inside the workspace, mounts a code body with the instance's props. When a project writes code for a design-backed component, that is a one-time port of the body; the record switches to `code=`, the tree body is deleted, and the instances do not change. Existing code is never recreated on the canvas: the file is the component, and the library record for it is a signature, not a copy.
10	
11	## 1. The document: one tree, written as markup
12	
13	Decision from the second spec, unchanged: a node tree stored in the artifact's Yjs doc (`nodes`), serialised for agents and for files as HTML-shaped markup with stable node ids, rendered by CawCo to HTML/CSS. Why: agents write HTML-shaped markup best and patch by id precisely (pen's MCP shape); a fixed flex vocabulary draws the same in every WebKit and Blink web view (own knowledge; probe 1); every node type has a direct SwiftUI, Flutter, React Native and web form, which raw HTML/CSS does not; OpenUI Lang is an app-view language with queries and tools, not a design document.
14	
15	Node types: `design` (root; `tokens=` names the token CSS), `artboard` (device preset phone|tablet|desktop|free, width), `frame` (`layout` row|column|free, `gap`, `pad`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `width`/`height` fixed|hug|fill, `fill`, `stroke`, `radius`, `shadow`, `clip`, `scroll`, `hidden`), `text` (`style`, `color`, `align`, `lines`, content), `image` (`asset`, `fit`), `icon` (set name; CawCo's own is Solar duotone), `instance` (`of`, prop values, children fill the default slot, `slot=` names another), `slot` (a named hole inside a design body), `override` (design-backed only, §2), `note` (annotation, never ported). `choice`/`option` on any node for picks (D19). Values are token names from `design/` (or CawCo's neutral base set for a project without one); a raw value is drawn and marked "untokened". Unknown component or token: refused by name (the mockup library's rule, kept). The hub assigns ids to nodes written without one and answers the markup with ids filled in (D25's rule).
16	
17	Example, a code project:
18	
19	```html
20	<design name="transcript-cards" tokens="apps/dashboard/src/lib/tokens/tokens.css">
21	  <artboard id="a1" name="Density" device="desktop" width="960">
22	    <frame id="a1.row" layout="row" gap="s4" pad="s4">
23	      <instance id="a1.c1" of="EventCard" density="compact" event="fixture:./cards.fixtures.ts#toolCall"
24	                choice="density" option="compact"/>
25	      <instance id="a1.c2" of="EventCard" density="roomy" event="fixture:./cards.fixtures.ts#failed"
26	                choice="density" option="roomy">
27	        <text id="a1.c2.b" slot="footer" style="mono" color="ink-2">error TS2345 at src/x.ts:12</text>
28	      </instance>
29	    </frame>
30	    <note id="a1.n1" at="a1.c2">Roomy shows the error's first line in full.</note>
31	  </artboard>
32	</design>
33	```
34	
35	Files: the Yjs doc is the truth while the design is worked on; `artifact_promote` writes `design/<name>.design.html`. The library is `design/components/<Name>.design.html`, one file per component record (§2).
36	
37	## 2. The component contract (one model, two bodies)
38	
39	A **component record**:
40	
41	```html
42	<component id="EventCard"
43	           props="density: compact|roomy = compact; event: json; status: ok|error|running = ok"
44	           slots="footer"
45	           code="apps/dashboard/src/lib/cawco/transcript/EventCard.svelte"/>
46	```
47	
48	or, before code exists:
49	
50	```html
51	<component id="Button" props="kind: primary|secondary|ghost = primary; label: text; disabled: bool = false" slots="leading">
52	  <frame id="b.root" layout="row" gap="s1" pad="s2 s3" fill="{kind == primary ? accent : surface}" radius="r2">
53	    <slot id="b.lead" name="leading"/>
54	    <text id="b.label" style="label" color="{kind == primary ? on-accent : ink-1}">{label}</text>
55	  </frame>
56	</component>
57	```
58	
59	- **Props**: `text`, `number`, `bool`, enum (`a|b|c` — the variants, Figma's variant properties (own knowledge)), token types (`color`, `space`, `style`), `image`, `json`. Each has a default. A `json` or any prop may take `fixture:<path>#<export>`, a value imported from a project file by the host (code projects only).
60	- **Slots**: named holes; an instance's children fill them. A design body declares them with `slot` nodes; a code body's slots are the file's children/snippets/`@ViewBuilder`s, named in `slots=`.
61	- **Instance**: `of`, prop values (unspecified → defaults), slot children. Editing the component changes every instance; there is no copy anywhere.
62	- **Override** (`override node= prop= value=`): allowed only on an instance of a **design-backed** component, addressing a descendant node of its body (pen's `descendants`). A code body has no addressable inner nodes, so its variation is props and slots only. This asymmetry is what makes the handover (§4) a defined step rather than a leak.
63	- **Body**: `design` (the tree inside the record) or `code` (`code=` path; the framework is read from the file's extension and the Vite root's `package.json`). Exactly one; never both. Nothing in the contract names the body except `code=`.
64	- **Library**: `design/components/*` plus CawCo's base records (button, input, toggle, checkbox, select, tabs, dialog, toast, list row, avatar, badge, device frames: the mockup primitives, as design bodies). The hub builds the library and the agent's prompt from it by content hash (the `mockups.ts` mechanism, moved to `design-library.ts`). For a code project, a record with `code=` is **declared**, not copied: an agent reads the file's props and writes the signature line — the same as a `.d.ts` or Storybook's argTypes, with none of the body. Later: the host derives the signature from the file where the framework exposes it (Svelte's `$props()` type, Vue's `defineProps`, React's TS props), triggered when the owner wants declarations to stop being manual.
65	
66	The record switches body exactly once in its life, design → code (§4). It never goes back: once code exists, the file is the component.
67	
68	## 3. Rendering: one renderer, two mount paths, the venue follows the components
69	
70	The renderer is one framework-free script, shipped in the overlay (which already runs inside the shadow-root host and inside every preview iframe). It walks the tree and draws frames, text, images, icons and notes to DOM with the token CSS and fonts loaded. For an `instance` it does one of two things:
71	
72	- **Design-backed**: expands the body with the instance's props and overrides, recursively. Pure DOM; no project code.
73	- **Code-backed**: leaves a mount point carrying the props and asks the **stage host** to mount the real file into it.
74	
75	**Venue.** A project with no code renders in the dashboard's shadow-root host (the mockup library's, kept) — always live, nothing to start. A project with code renders at `/__cawco/design/<artifact-id>` on the stage host, so the project's framework, modules, token CSS and fonts are present; the same renderer script runs there under the overlay.
76	
77	**The stage host** (the first spec, kept whole; condensed here): the daemon on the workspace's machine runs the project's own Vite programmatically from the workspace's own `node_modules` (`createServer({ configFile: <project's>, plugins: [cawcoDesign(), ...] })`; inline plugins merge with the config file's: own knowledge, probe 2), with the runtime the project's lockfile implies (`bun` or `node`), inside the workspace sandbox, as a listener the supervisor owns: start on first use, `ready` within 60 s, health every 15 s, restart ×3 with backoff then `error`, asleep after 30 min idle, wake on open, stop on archive. One embedded `host.mjs` in CawCo's binary, written to `.cawco/stage/` (git-excluded); nothing installed into the project; refused by name if no Vite root, no `vite`, or no runtime. Our plugin serves the design page (an HTML shell from the app's own `app.html`/`index.html`), a virtual module `cawco:mount?components=EventCard,StatusDot` that imports each code-backed component's file and the fixtures the instances name, an event relay (`ready`, `update`, `error {file,line,column,message,frame}`, `clear`) on stdout, and, for frameworks without dev metadata, the vendored code-inspector transforms (MIT per the research report). Vite's error overlay is off; ours shows.
78	
79	**Mount adapters** (the only per-framework code, inside `host.mjs`): Svelte `mount(Component, { target, props })`; Vue `createApp`; React `createRoot`; Solid `render`; Preact `render`. **Slots**: the instance's slot children are neutral nodes the renderer draws; the adapter passes them as the framework's children: Svelte through `createRawSnippet` rendering a placeholder the renderer then fills (own knowledge that Svelte 5 exports `createRawSnippet`; probe 3); React as a `children` element holding a ref'd container; Vue as a render-function slot. **HMR**: the adapter accepts module updates and re-mounts the affected instances with the same props (`import.meta.hot.accept`, own knowledge; probe 2), so editing the real file re-draws every instance in place, state of the rest of the canvas untouched. **Props** that cross from the tree to the component are JSON, token names (passed as the token's string), or fixture exports.
80	
81	Panel states for a code project: Starting ("Starting Vite in `apps/dashboard`…"), Compiling (progress line, last render stays), Error (message, `file:line:column`, frame, over the dimmed render; also delivered to the agent within 3 s), Live, Asleep ("Waking…"). A no-code design has only Live.
82	
83	## 4. The one-time handover: design body → code body
84	
85	Trigger: the project starts writing code, or the owner says "build this". An agent (an ordinary coding task, guided by the `port-design` skill, D14) writes the component's code **once** from the design body, keeping the contract: same name, same prop names and enum values, same slot names, tokens by role. The emitted file carries its origin (`<!-- design: Button -->`, or the language's comment form). Then the switch, which the hub performs and gates:
86	
87	1. The agent calls `component_switch(name, code: <path>)` (or writes `code=` on the record through `artifact_update`; one tool, the same check).
88	2. **Override check.** The hub lists every `override` in use on instances of this component. The switch is refused while any remains: an override addresses inner nodes that will not exist. The agent resolves each by one of two patches: expose a prop (`titleColor: color`) in the code and rewrite those overrides as prop values on the instances (a hub patch by id, listed in the refusal), or detach that instance. No silent drop.
89	3. **Mount check.** The stage host compiles the file and mounts it once per instance with that instance's props and slots. Any compile or mount error returns `{file, line, column, message}` and the switch stays refused.
90	4. **Parity render.** Every artboard that uses the component is drawn twice — the design body and the code body — and pixel-diffed per instance (the probe kit's `pixelmatch` with the design's threshold). The result opens as a before/after artifact with the per-instance diff percentages; the verifier session (§5.7, never the builder) judges it, and the person can look. Acceptance is explicit: the agent passes the verifier's verdict to `component_switch(..., accept: true)`.
91	5. **Switch.** In one Yjs transaction: `code=` is set, the tree body is deleted, `ported="<framework>: <path> @ <commit>"` is recorded on the record. The instances are untouched: `of`, props, slots and ids are the same bytes. From this transaction the renderer takes the code path for them.
92	
93	Nothing is ever rendered from both bodies at once except inside step 4. There is no way back to a design body; a change to the component after the switch is a change to the file, by the agent, on a pin.
94	
95	A whole artboard ported as a screen becomes a code-backed component record of its own (`Screen.svelte` with the instances inside it); its instances on other artboards follow the same rule. Ports to a second target (SwiftUI, Flutter, React Native) add a second `ported=` entry; the canvas draws the one the project's stage host can run (the web one) and the others are proven on their platforms as today (simulator snapshots per the first spec's coverage note). The mapping table from the second spec (frame → HStack/VStack, Row/Column, flex View, flex div; slot → `@ViewBuilder`, widget parameter, `children`, Snippet; tokens → the target's token file) lives in the skill.
96	
97	Traceability after the switch: `artifact_read(since: <the switch's cursor>)` lists the nodes changed since, which is the next coding task's work list; a pin on an instance names the file and, for a tap inside a rendered code instance, the exact `file:line:column` (§5).
98	
99	## 5. Editing and pins
100	
101	**The person, on the canvas** (own pan-and-zoom surface; no library: Excalidraw does not lay out flex DOM, Penpot is a whole application (own knowledge)):
102	- Select by tap, deeper by tap again, Esc up. Move (reorder inside flex with an insertion line; `x`/`y` in free frames; arrow-key nudge by one spacing step), resize (fixed; the inspector switches hug/fill), text in place, spacing/radius/colour through the token scale in the inspector (right panel; bottom sheet on phones), variant and other props as controls, swap instance, undo through `Y.UndoManager` scoped to the person's transactions (own knowledge of Yjs).
103	- **Design-backed component**: all of the above also inside the body (editing the master; every instance follows), and overrides on an instance's descendants.
104	- **Code-backed component**: props, slots, position and variant on the instance; a tap inside its render selects the inner element and the edit is a **pin**, because the inside is the file. Direct in-place edits of a code body's internals (text, spacing, colour) are not built; if the owner wants them later, they become edit-proposal pins `{file, line, column, property, from, to}` the agent applies — never an AST write-back by CawCo (the research report: no formatting-preserving printer for Svelte; Glide's regex path "too fragile").
105	
106	**Pins, comments, ink** on any artifact, one payload: `{ node, component?, source? }` — `node` is the canvas node id (stable across edits; the "moved" tray is for deleted nodes); `component` is the record the node is inside; `source` is present when the tap landed inside a code-backed render: `{file, line, column}` from `__svelte_meta.loc` (+1, 0-based per the research report; refreshed from the DOM after every HMR update) or from `data-insp-path`. A comment therefore reads either "`a1.c2` (EventCard, roomy): tighter" or "`EventCard.svelte:42:6` inside `a1.c2`: heavier". Desktop taps on a `file:line` open the editor through Vite's `/__open-in-editor` on the host (own knowledge that Vite serves it; probe 2).
107	
108	**The agent, through tools:**
109	
110	| Tool | For a design |
111	|---|---|
112	| `artifact_create` | `kind: "design"`, `name`, `markup`. Answers id, route, markup with ids; refuses unknown components or tokens by name; parse errors with line. |
113	| `artifact_update` | `markup` merged by node id (nodes with the same id updated in place; selection, pins and unsent person edits survive — the tree's idiomorph), or `patch` by node id: `set`, `insert`, `move`, `delete`, `override`. Answers the markup after the change and the nodes the person changed since the last read, flagged. |
114	| `artifact_read` | Markup with ids, untokened nodes, pins, comments, picks, `changed` since a cursor, host `status`/`errors` for a code project; `png: true` renders the artboards (viewer render, or the hub's headless render; probe 5 decides the mechanism). |
115	| `design_library` | The project's component records: name, props, slots, body kind (`design`/`code`), `ported`. |
116	| `component_switch` | §4's handover: the override list, mount errors, the parity artifact, and the switch on `accept`. |
117	| `artifact_show`, `artifact_promote`, `comment_*` | Unchanged. Promote writes the design and its records to `design/`. |
118	
119	Person edits reach the agent as today: batched after 3 s of quiet, at once during the turn; "Send N" for pins and picks. Host status and errors ride the same channel.

122	
123	- **Replaced**: the OpenUI mockup library (`@cawco/core/mockups`, hub `mockups.ts`, `views/openui/mockup`, `system: "cawco"`, specimen templates). Its host, token loading, manifest and refuse-by-name are kept as the design renderer's; its primitives become base records; CawCo's own dashboard components become code-backed records in the cockpit repo's `design/components/` (declared signatures, no copies). Cutover, not alongside.
124	- **Kept**: OpenUI for live agent-made views with data (blocks, "Ask Caw for a view"); `page`, `canvas` (Excalidraw drawing), `preview` (a running app or folder, unchanged); the Yjs doc, pins, comments, picks, dials, ink, delivery, the panel.
125	- **Dropped**: "an agent reads an existing component and recreates it on the canvas" — in a code project the file is the component, and the only thing an agent writes about it is its signature line. The agent-written `.stage.svelte` from the first spec is gone too: the artboard is the stage, generated by the host from the tree.
126	- **Later, and what triggers it**: signature derivation from source (when manual declarations annoy); edit-proposal pins for code internals (if the owner asks); Script nodes (pen's live layers) when a design needs motion or data; Flutter through `flutter widget-preview start` and the simulator snapshot host for SwiftUI/Compose, when a project on those stacks wants its instances drawn rather than only ported.

128	## 7. The transcript cards, as it goes under this spec
129	
130	`EventCard` and `StatusDot` are code-backed records (two signature lines). One design, one artboard, two instances with `density` as the pick, fixtures from the existing `cards.fixtures.ts`. The host mounts the real `EventCard.svelte` twice; the owner picks on the iPad and pins the roomy title; the agent edits `EventCard.svelte:42`; HMR re-draws both instances. Zero re-coded lines, no dev route, no server for the agent to keep alive.

132	## 8. What must be proven first
133	
134	1. **Renderer parity across engines** (no-code path): three base records on an artboard, rendered in Chrome and the iPad web view; pixel diff < 0.5 %, differences only in text antialiasing. Fail → remove the engine-dependent property from the vocabulary.
135	2. **Code-backed mount under SvelteKit**: from `apps/dashboard`, the host serves the design page through the hub proxy; `EventCard.svelte` mounted twice with the instances' props and a fixture import; `$lib`, `app.css`, Tailwind resolve; an edit to the file re-draws both instances in < 1 s without reload; five inner elements' `__svelte_meta.loc` + 1 match the source; `/__open-in-editor` opens the file. Record whether `$app/state`'s `page` throws outside kit's root.
136	3. **Slots across the boundary**: a neutral `text` child in an instance's `footer` slot renders inside the Svelte component's snippet via `createRawSnippet`; the same for a React project's `children`. Fail → slot children for code bodies are limited to text and image until a per-framework path exists; said so, not hidden.
137	4. **Handover on one component**: a design-backed `Button` with two instances, one carrying an override; the switch refuses with the override listed; after the prop patch, the parity artifact shows two diffs under threshold; `accept` deletes the body and the instances render from code with the same ids.
138	5. **Headless render**: `artifact_read(png: true)` with no viewer attached, within 2 s per artboard; the probe records which mechanism it took.
139	6. **Lifecycle**: the host alive 30 min after the session's last turn; after `kill -9`, the next open renders within the warm budget; asleep and wake as specified.

Never use the claude-in-chrome tools.

## What CawCo is
A self-hosted control plane for AI coding agents: a `cawco` daemon on each machine, a hub, and a browser dashboard (SvelteKit, in this repo at apps/dashboard) plus an iOS/iPad app whose session screens show the same web content in a web view. Each agent session has an artifact panel (pages, previews of running apps, an Excalidraw canvas) where the person pins comments, picks between options, draws with the Apple Pencil, and the agent reads all of it back. Delegated agents work inside "workspaces": a git clone of the project in a sandbox the daemon owns; a workspace's dev server port is shown in the panel through the hub's preview proxy (packages/hub/src/preview.ts, packages/agent/src/preview.ts). The daemon is a compiled Bun binary.

## The feature, in the owner's words (verbatim, in order)
- "Are you not able to dynamically create and render svelte components in the preview?"
- "I already told the original prd that that's what I want something how pen or paper does it"
- "They use jsx mainly but I don't want jsx"
- He linked github.com/mateothegreat/svelte-dynamic-component-engine and github.com/kenoxa/svelte-jsx: "lookup newer ones"
- "are there systems, libraries or people who have done this already instead of us handrolling? did you even do your research? can u reuse componetns and assemble t hem and edit them?"
- "did you even lookup what pen, paper, and similar products do it?"
- "remember this needs to work for all our users, across their many languages and frameworks"
- "so what's the best technical solution ehre"
- "No dude, are you unable to have reusable components without having the agent rewrite it which leads to the defects this w hi Ole thing was made to prevent"
- "Isn't there an existing standard"
- "Ur not going to rewrite figma from scratch with a propeiatry design format are you?"
- "Can u stop jumping to action and actually stop, research and think and Wright the options before jumping to code, Jesus"
- In a questionnaire he raised: pure-design projects that have no Vite (no code yet); components should be "just components and agnostic"; and "v1/v2" labels are jargon to him — use plain words.

The defect that started this (PRD decision log, 2026-10-16): a redesign of the transcript cards spent about 3.5 hours on preview plumbing — workspace dev servers dying between turns, copies synced to a host server, and about 15,000 lines of card variants re-coded in a dev route instead of reusing the real `transcript/*.svelte` components.

## What he picked
He was given four options and answered "Ok do C", then "Ask fable to flesh it out and see what's the best practice and approach here". The options were:
- A. Penpot as the design surface, via its MCP server.
- B. Bring your own design tool over its MCP (the PRD's D18, "No adapters").
- C. **Real code components: the agent composes the project's real components; CawCo runs the project's own dev toolchain (Vite first) and keeps it alive; a click on the render maps to `file:line:column`.**
- D. A catalog of components (A2UI / OpenUI) — stays for agent-made data views, not this.
The lead's recommendation alongside was: C for projects with code, B or A for design-only work, W3C Design Tokens (format 2025.10) everywhere. He picked C without ruling on the design-only case.

Penpot's checked caveats, for context on why A lost: no iPad/Pencil support (issues #6394, #3810, #2102), no supported embedding (#11735), its MCP needs a person's browser tab open with the plugin, code export stops at web HTML/CSS, real code components can't be imported, and self-hosting is a multi-service Docker stack.

## Rejected already — do not bring back
- A CawCo-owned design markup and renderer (a node tree with artboards/frames/overrides drawn by CawCo): he called that rewriting Figma with a proprietary format.
- Compiling Svelte inside CawCo's binary (Bun.build + svelte/compiler, REPL-style): it can't see the project's config (aliases, Tailwind, `$app`) and covers Svelte only.
- Running Storybook itself as the renderer: needs per-framework Storybook packages installed into the project. (Whether Storybook's *file format* is the standard he asked about is open — see Q1.)
- An agent reading an existing component and recreating it anywhere.

## Read first (all readable from your workspace)
1. The PRD, in your clone: `.design-foundations/plans/2026-10-06-projects.md`. Read §4's table rows D18, D19, D24–D29; §5.7 "Design work"; §5.10 "Artifacts" whole, including the "Live components (D29)" paragraph near its end; and §11's decision log entries dated 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-16. D29's text still says "Svelte only" and "No dev server for the agent to keep alive"; his later words above widen it to every framework, and C answers the dev-server complaint by having CawCo, not the agent, keep the toolchain alive. Reconcile these.

The prior-art report (read whole): `/home/bewinxed/.local/share/cawco/projects/70ac3d41-5a28-4a31-8e9e-3be2b03d1516/assets/22627679/docs/research/live-components-prior-art.md` — Onlook, Storybook Svelte CSF, poveste, vite-plugin-svelte's inspector and `__svelte_meta`, stylewright, Glide, code-inspector (MIT; `data-insp-path` stamping for 7 frameworks and 7 bundlers), Storybook CSF and portable stories, Onlook's desktop app (runs the project's own dev command in a worktree), non-web stacks.

Its design-body half (§1, design bodies in §2, §4's handover) is the rejected proprietary path. Its code-body half — §3's stage host (programmatic Vite with an added plugin, lifecycle, mount adapters, HMR, error relay), §5's pins carrying `{file,line,column}`, and §8's probes — is the starting detail for C. ## What the prior-art report did not cover — look these up
- Products that let people assemble a project's **registered real code components** into screens and edit their props visually: e.g. Plasmic code components, Builder.io registered components / Fusion, Webflow code components (DevLink), Framer code components, Figma Code Connect, Subframe, Paper's "use your code components" roadmap item, pen.dev. For each that applies: how components are registered, how their props are described (schema source), where the composed screen is stored (code in the repo vs the tool's JSON), which frameworks, and how the person edits.
- Storybook's Component Story Format: whether CSF is a published open standard (componentdriven.org / github.com/ComponentDriven/csf), what CSF 3 and the newer CSF factories define (args, argTypes, render), and who consumes it besides Storybook (Ladle, Chromatic, Playwright component tests via portable stories, others). This is the strongest candidate for his "Isn't there an existing standard" — judge it on the facts.
- Element-to-source mapping per framework today, including whether React 19 removed `_debugSource` and what click-to-component tools use now; Vue's inspector; Angular.
- Running a project's toolchain for many stacks (Vite, Next.js/Turbopack, webpack, Angular CLI, Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit): injecting a plugin programmatically versus running the project's own dev command and injecting a client script, and how existing tools add their transform without editing the user's config.
- Deriving a component's props from source: TS-based tools (react-docgen-typescript, vue-component-meta, svelte2tsx / Svelte's `$props()` types, Storybook's argTypes inference).
Read each source you rely on whole, not just a search highlight.

1. **Composition.** Where a composed screen or variant sheet lives and in what format — a file in the project's own language, CSF, or something else — given "components just components and agnostic", no proprietary format, no JSX in a Svelte project. Who writes it, and how the person's canvas edits (order, variant, props, slot content) reach it.
2. **Running it.** How CawCo runs the project's toolchain across frameworks and keeps it alive with no agent involved (start, health, sleep, wake, restart, errors to the agent with `file:line:column`), inside the workspace sandbox, shown through the hub's preview proxy on desktop and in the iPad's web view.
3. **The canvas.** How instances and variants sit side by side the way pen.dev and Paper show them, and how D19 picks, pins, comments and Pencil ink (D24–D27) work on top.
4. **Source mapping** per framework, and exactly what a pin carries.
5. **Editing.** What the person edits directly versus what becomes a pin the agent acts on (component internals), with what established tools do for each.
6. **Knowing the components.** How CawCo learns a project's components and their props without anyone re-declaring them by hand.
7. **Projects with no code yet** under C. Lay out the options honestly.
8. **Non-web stacks** (SwiftUI, Flutter, Compose, React Native): what C gives them.
9. **Tokens:** where the W3C Design Tokens format fits.
10. **What it replaces** in CawCo today (the "dev server or folder" preview as the way an agent shows a component; the OpenUI mockup library from 2026-10-15 in the decision log; D29's "Svelte only" text). CawCo's rule is cutover: one path, the old one deleted, no fallbacks unless the owner authorises one — if a fallback looks needed, write it as a one-line question for him.
11. The rewritten PRD row for D29 and its §5.10 paragraph, ready to paste.

A separate spike (Opus, in workspace fd865b51) is measuring on CawCo's own dashboard: (1) SvelteKit's Vite driven programmatically with an added plugin serving a mount page — whether `$lib`, `$app/*`, Tailwind and tokens resolve and kit's handler leaves `/__cawco/*` alone; (2) HMR latency, and HMR through a path-prefixed reverse proxy like the hub's; (3) `__svelte_meta.loc` accuracy and the `parent` chain to the call site, and `/__open-in-editor`; (4) compile errors captured as JSON and cleared; (5) node vs bun, and whether the compiled Bun binary can `import()` an `.mjs` written at runtime; (6) code-inspector's transform injected into fresh Vite React and Vue apps without editing their configs. One normal commit, 3d27444ab, rebased onto origin/main. It replaces all of the branch's hold: commits.

**Switching tabs.** Each side of a tab is its curved "C": the flared foot, the flank and the shoulder. The selected tab is drawn on top of both neighbours. A clicked switch takes 400ms on the existing ease-in-out curve (`--choose-dur` / `--choose-ease`):
- First half: the side that will end up underneath folds its foot in and steps back 8px (one flare), onto the edge of the tab behind it.

1	# Live components, option C: the project's real components, run by the project's own toolchain
2	
3	Spec for PRD D29 after the owner's pick ("Ok do C"). Written 2026-10-16 from the PRD (§4 D18, D19, D24–D29; §5.7; §5.10; §11 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-16), the prior-art report (`assets/22627679/docs/research/live-components-prior-art.md`), the merged spec (`assets/8866317b/live-components-merged-spec.md`), and the sources cited inline. A claim with no URL is marked **own call**. Decisions that wait on the Opus spike in workspace fd865b51 are marked **spike (n)** with the branch taken if the answer is "no".
4	
5	## 0. The invariant, and the answer in one paragraph
6	
7	**A component exists once, as the project's real file. Everything the panel shows is an instance of that file, mounted by the project's own toolchain.** Nothing is re-coded per variant, per screen, or per render; nothing is described twice in a second format.
8	
9	The answer: a **sheet** is a Component Story Format (CSF 3) file next to the component, in the project's own language (`EventCard.stories.ts`, no JSX in a Svelte project): a default export naming the component, one named export per variant with its `args`. A **screen** is a real component in the project (`Screen.svelte`, `Screen.tsx`, `Screen.vue`) that composes other real components, and it gets a sheet like any component. The daemon runs the project's own dev toolchain inside the workspace (Vite first; Astro, Nuxt and Next through their programmatic APIs) with one CawCo plugin added at start, keeps it alive with no agent involved, and serves a page that mounts every story of a sheet side by side. The hub shows that page through the preview proxy it already has, with the overlay it already injects: picks, pins, comments and Pencil ink work on it unchanged. A tap inside a render carries `file:line:column` from the framework's own dev metadata (Svelte) or from a `data-insp-path` stamp (React, Vue, Solid, Preact, Qwik, Astro). The person edits props and variants directly (CawCo writes `args` back into the story file, as Storybook's "save from controls" does); everything inside a component or a screen template is a pin the agent acts on. CawCo learns components and their props from source with each framework's docgen. There is no CawCo design format, no mockup library, no handover.
10	
11	## 1. Composition: where a screen or a variant sheet lives, and in what format
12	
13	**Recommendation.** Two file kinds, both the project's own code, nothing else:
14	
15	| Thing | File | Format | Who writes it |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| Variant sheet (one component, N states) | `<Component>.stories.ts` (or `.js`) beside the component | CSF 3: `export default { component }`, `export const Roomy = { args: {…} }` | The agent; `args` also written by CawCo from the person's edits (§5) |
18	| Screen (several components composed) | `<Screen>.svelte` / `.tsx` / `.vue` wherever the project keeps screens | The framework's own component | The agent, from pins |
19	| States of a screen | `<Screen>.stories.ts` | CSF 3, same as above | The agent and CawCo |
20	
21	A story's `args` are the instance's props; a `render` is allowed only in the framework's own idiom (Svelte: `render: (args) => ({ Component, props: args })`; React: JSX, because JSX is that project's language). Slot content in a sheet is either a string prop (an arg) or belongs in a screen component.
22	
23	**Why CSF.** It is the one existing, non-proprietary, cross-framework format for "this component in this state", and it is already the project's language:
24	
25	- Its home repo defines it as "an open standard for UI component examples based on JavaScript ES6 modules", "Non-proprietary. CSF doesn't require any vendor-specific libraries", and lists consumers beyond Storybook: "Tools: Storybook, WebComponents.dev, Components.studio, RedwoodJS, UXPin" (https://github.com/ComponentDriven/csf). Judged on the facts: it is a de-facto standard owned by Storybook (the repo note says its code "lives in the Storybook monorepo"), not a W3C or ECMA document. It is still the only format with more than one implementation.
26	- Storybook: "It's an open standard based on ES6 modules that is portable beyond Storybook"; the default export's `component` field "is required and used by addons for automatic prop table generation"; stories are objects: `export const Primary: Story = { args: { primary: true } }` (https://storybook.js.org/docs/api/csf).
27	- Other consumers: Ladle "supports Component Story Format … developed as a drop-in replacement of Storybook" (https://ladle.dev/blog/introducing-ladle/; React only); portable stories "convert this story context into an appropriately renderable component … a React story becomes a React component, a Vue story becomes a Vue component" for Playwright CT, Vitest and Jest (https://storybook.js.org/blog/portable-stories-for-playwright-ct/); Chromatic snapshots stories (https://chromatic.com/docs/storybook).
28	- CSF Next (factories: `definePreview → preview.meta → meta.story`) is "a preview feature and (though unlikely) the API may change" (https://storybook.js.org/docs/api/csf/csf-next). CawCo reads CSF 3 and does not emit CSF Next until it leaves preview. **Own call.**
29	
30	**Why not JSX in Svelte.** The owner's rule, and CSF does not need it: a Svelte story is `args` on a `component`; a composition is a `.svelte` file. `@storybook/addon-svelte-csf`'s `.stories.svelte` syntax is not used: it is a Vite plugin plus runtime that must be installed into the project (prior-art report §2), and CSF `.stories.ts` is the same shape in every framework. One path.
31	
32	**Why not a CawCo tree, Plasmic/Builder JSON, or pen.dev's `.pen`.** Plasmic and Builder store the composed screen in their own cloud JSON and render it through an "app host" page in the user's React app (Plasmic: "The app host will run Plasmic Studio within your React app", https://docs.plasmic.app/learn/code-components/); Webflow DevLink and Framer only take components registered with a declaration file or `addPropertyControls` (https://developers.webflow.com/code-components/importing/quick-start.md, https://www.framer.com/developers/property-controls); pen.dev's "Code → Design: Recreate existing components on the pen.dev canvas" is the recreation the owner rejected (https://docs.pencil.dev/design-and-code/design-to-code); Paper's "Use your code components" is a roadmap item (https://paper.design/roadmap). Every one of them is React-only or recreates. CSF needs none of that.
33	
34	**A project that already has Storybook** already has sheets: CawCo lists its `*.stories.*` files and mounts them. Project-level decorators from `.storybook/preview` are not applied: portable stories docs, "The project-level annotations … are not applied automatically" (https://storybook.js.org/docs/8/api/portable-stories/portable-stories-playwright). A component that needs one (a theme provider) names it in the sheet's `decorators`, which CawCo does apply, story-level and meta-level. **Own call.**
35	
36	**How the person's edits reach the file.** Props, variant, slot text that is a prop: CawCo rewrites that story's `args` object literal in place (§5). Order of stories, a new story, a duplicate, a deleted story: CawCo edits the exports (append, remove, reorder) the way Storybook does — "The new or modified story will appear as a code change in that component's CSF file and will be automatically formatted to match the code style and formatting of your project" (https://storybook.js.org/blog/interactive-story-generation/). Everything inside a component or a screen's template is a pin for the agent (choice 1 in "Choices for the owner" is whether CawCo also splices templates).
37	
38	## 2. Running it: the stage
39	
40	**Recommendation.** One **stage** per workspace, owned by the daemon's supervisor, running the project's own toolchain in the project's own runtime inside the workspace sandbox, with one CawCo plugin added at start and nothing installed into the project.
41	
42	**Start.** The daemon writes `.cawco/stage/host.mjs` (CawCo's embedded script, git-excluded) and spawns it with the runtime the lockfile implies: `bun` if `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`, else `node`. The host runs in the project's runtime and imports the project's own `vite`/`astro`/`nuxt`/`next` from the workspace's `node_modules`; CawCo's binary only supervises. **Own call**, and it makes spike (5)'s question (can the compiled Bun binary `import()` a runtime-written `.mjs`?) moot: the binary never imports the toolchain. If the spike shows the binary can, the design stays as written: the project's Vite version must not be coupled to CawCo's process.
43	
44	**Per toolchain, how the plugin gets in without editing the user's config:**
45	
46	| Toolchain | How the host starts it | Source |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| Vite (incl. SvelteKit, Vue, React, Solid, Preact, Qwik, Lit) | `createServer({ configFile: <project's>, plugins: [cawcoStage()] })`; inline config is merged with the file's | Vite JavaScript API: `createServer(inlineConfig)`, "any valid user config options, plus `mode` and `configFile`" (https://vite.dev/guide/api-javascript). Storybook does the same: "it automatically merges the configuration into its own" (https://storybook.js.org/docs/builders/vite). **Spike (1)**: does SvelteKit's handler leave `/__cawco/*` alone and do `$lib`, `$app/*`, Tailwind and tokens resolve? If "no": the stage serves its page from its own Connect middleware registered before kit's (`configureServer` with `server.middlewares.use` at `enforce: 'pre'`), and `$app/*` imports inside components are shimmed by the plugin for the stage page only. Bring that branch to the owner before building, because it touches how kit components behave outside kit. |
49	| Astro | `dev({ root, vite: { plugins: [cawcoStage()] } })` | "Programmatic Astro API (experimental)": `dev(inlineConfig: AstroInlineConfig) => Promise<DevServer>` (https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/programmatic-reference/). Experimental: pinned per Astro major, re-checked on upgrade. |
50	| Nuxt | `loadNuxt({ dev: true, overrides: { modules: [cawcoNuxtModule] } })`, the module calling `addVitePlugin` | Nuxt Kit `loadNuxt(loadOptions)`, "`overrides`: Configuration applied above every layer, including the root project's own `nuxt.config`" (https://nuxt.com/docs/api/kit/programmatic) |
51	| Next.js | `next({ dev: true, dir, conf: { ...loaded, turbopack: { rules: codeInspectorPlugin({ bundler: 'turbopack' }) } } })` and `app.getRequestHandler()` | Custom server: `conf` is "The same object you would use in `next.config.js`" (https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/custom-server); code-inspector's Turbopack form for Next ≥ 15.3 is `turbopack: { rules: codeInspectorPlugin({ bundler: 'turbopack' }) }` (https://www.npmjs.com/package/vite-code-inspector-plugin). The stage page is served by the host's own HTTP handler in front of Next's request handler, and it imports the story module through Next's dev compiler; no route or file is added to the project. **Spike (6)** covers code-inspector in fresh Vite React/Vue apps, not Next; Next is a second probe before it is promised. |
52	| Angular CLI, plain webpack, anything else | **Refused by name**: "Live components need a Vite, Astro, Nuxt or Next.js dev toolchain; this project uses Angular CLI." | Angular's `ng serve` has no public plugin API; the two tools that stamp Angular templates do it by a custom builder in `angular.json` ("This uses a custom dev-server builder to inject `data-click-to-source` into templates", https://github.com/mattkawczynski/click-to-source) or by monkey-patching `fs.readFileSync` ("Intercepts Angular compiler's HTML template reads via `fs.readFileSync` monkey-patch", https://github.com/ALittleFox/dom-xray). Neither is a path CawCo should run in a user's project. If the owner wants these stacks shown without source mapping, that is the fallback question in §10. |
53	
54	**What the plugin serves** (kept from the merged spec §3, trimmed): `GET /__cawco/sheet?file=<repo-relative .stories.ts>` → an HTML shell built from the project's own `index.html`/`app.html` (so global CSS, fonts and tokens load), importing a virtual module `cawco:sheet?file=…` that imports the story file, reads `default.component`, `default.args`, `default.decorators`, and each named export's `args`/`render`/`decorators`, and mounts each story into its own frame with the framework's mount function. Mount adapters are the only per-framework code: Svelte `mount(Component, { target, props })`, Vue `createApp(Component, props).mount(target)`, React `createRoot(target).render(createElement(Component, props))`, Solid `render`, Preact `render`. HMR: the sheet module accepts updates (`import.meta.hot.accept`) and re-mounts affected frames with the same args; editing `EventCard.svelte` redraws every instance in place. **Spike (2)** measures HMR latency and HMR through the hub's proxy. If HMR does not pass the proxy: the plugin sets `server.hmr.path` and `clientPort` to the preview's own origin (the hub gives every preview "an origin of its own, never the dashboard's", `packages/hub/src/preview.ts`), so no path prefix is involved.
55	
56	**Lifecycle** (one supervisor rule set, no agent in the loop): start on the first `artifact_create(kind: "sheet")` or first open; `ready` within 60 s or `error`; health `GET /__cawco/health` every 15 s; restart ×3 with backoff then `error`; asleep after 30 min with no viewer and no agent read; wake on open; stop when the workspace is archived. Panel states: Starting ("Starting vite in `apps/dashboard`…"), Compiling, Error, Live, Asleep ("Waking…"). The stage listens on a port inside the workspace and is shown through the existing `port:<port>@<workspace>` preview source (`packages/agent/src/preview-bridge.ts`), so desktop and the iPad's web view get the same overlay-injected page.
57	
58	**Errors to the agent.** The plugin turns Vite's error payload (`message`, `loc: { file, line, column }`, `frame`) into `status.errors` on the artifact; the hub delivers it on the same batched channel as pins (3 s quiet, at once during a turn). The overlay draws CawCo's error card over the dimmed last render; Vite's own overlay is off (`server.hmr.overlay: false`). **Spike (4)** proves compile errors are captured as JSON and cleared on the next good compile. If Vite's payload lacks `loc` for a framework, the error carries `file` from the failing module id and no line.
59	
60	## 3. The canvas: instances and variants side by side
61	
62	**Recommendation.** A sheet renders as one page: a horizontal row (wrapping) of frames, one frame per story, each labelled with the story's name, each hugging its content; a story's width is `parameters.viewport` when set (Storybook's own key), otherwise content width. This is what pen.dev and Paper show: component states laid out as separate frames on an artboard (Paper's documented workflow: "a `Component States` artboard detailing every default 
…[8779 chars clipped]…
CawCo's dependencies bundled into `host.mjs`, resolving `typescript`, `svelte`, `vue` from the project's `node_modules` (they are peer deps of those tools). To prove: that bundle runs in both `node` and `bun` against a project that has `typescript` installed; a project without `typescript` gets props from JSDoc only, said so in the inspector ("types unknown: add TypeScript or JSDoc"), not hidden.
124	
125	**Discovery.** Components are every `.svelte`/`.vue` file under the project's source root and every `.tsx`/`.jsx` with a capitalised export that docgen recognises, excluding routes (`routes/`, `pages/`, `app/` folders of the framework) and `node_modules`. The list and each file's props are cached by content hash and refreshed on that file's HMR update. Existing `*.stories.*` files are indexed as sheets. The agent reads it with `components_list` (§10's tools) and the dashboard's "Add story / New sheet" picker uses the same list. **Own call** on the globs; the precedent is Storybook's `stories` globs and vue-component-meta's "supports … components from `.vue`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, and `.jsx` files".
126	
127	## 7. Projects with no code yet
128	
129	Under C there is no second format to draw in, so a pure-design project has these options. The owner picks (choice 2 below).
130	
131	1. **Code from the first screen (recommended).** The person or Caw names the stack once (D18 already asks before building a design system); the agent scaffolds the project's framework with its own tool (`npm create vite@latest`, `npx sv create`, …) and every component is a real file from day one. Sheets, pins and picks apply at once; the first components are plain shapes and text. Costs: a framework is chosen before any pixel; a scaffold's `node_modules` in the workspace. Gives: no handover, ever; this spec's one path.
132	2. **A design tool over its MCP, as D18 already allows.** pen.dev or Paper as a project MCP server; explorations saved to `design/explorations/` with a link back; when code starts, the agent ports from the design file (pen.dev documents this: "Design → Code: Generate components from pen.dev designs", https://docs.pencil.dev/design-and-code/design-to-code). Costs: two truths until the port; the tool's own iPad/Pencil story (not checked here); the port is a one-time agent task per component. Gives: a drawing surface before any stack exists.
133	3. **Penpot (option A)** lost on the facts the owner already has (no iPad/Pencil, no embedding, a Docker stack). Not re-opened.
134	
135	A CawCo-owned design body for the no-code phase (the merged spec's §1–§2) stays rejected.
136	
137	## 8. Non-web stacks: what C gives them
138	
139	- **Flutter**: the stage is `flutter widget-preview start`, which "launches a local server and opens a real-time preview environment in your browser" for widgets marked `@Preview` (prior-art report §8, docs.flutter.dev). `@Preview` functions are Flutter's sheet; the daemon supervises the command like Vite; the overlay goes on top; pins carry the preview name, no `file:line` (Flutter renders to a canvas, there is no DOM to stamp). The API "is not stable and will change" (api.flutter.dev); pinned per Flutter release.
140	- **React Native**: through the web. Storybook's `react-native-web-vite` framework exists (prior-art report §7a); a RN project with `react-native-web` and Vite gets sheets, mapping and props like any React project. Without it: nothing.
141	- **SwiftUI, Compose**: nothing live. Their previews are IDE-bound (Xcode Previews, Android Studio; report §8). C gives them the *concept*: `#Preview` blocks and `@Preview` composables are the sheet, rendered on the Mac/simulator through the existing snapshot path (Anbar's probe kit), shown as pictures in the panel with pins by box; no source mapping. Said plainly in the panel: "Snapshot, not live".
142	
143	## 9. Tokens: where the W3C Design Tokens format fits
144	
145	The DTCG Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10 is the first stable version: "This specification is considered stable", a "Final Community Group Report 28 October 2025", JSON files, with reference implementations in "Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, and Terrazzo" and support from "Penpot, Figma, Sketch, Framer, Knapsack, Supernova, and zeroheight" (https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/; https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/2025/10/28/design-tokens-specification-reaches-first-stable-version/). It is not a W3C Recommendation ("It is not a W3C Standard nor is it on the W3C Standards Track").
146	
147	Where it fits, in three places and no more:
148	
149	1. **Rendering**: nowhere. A sheet renders with the project's real CSS; tokens reach it however the project ships them (CawCo's own: `design/tokens/cawco.tokens.json` → `bun run tokens` → `tokens.css`, per the repo's CLAUDE.md).
150	2. **The inspector**: a prop whose type is a colour, length or font role offers the names from the project's `**/*.tokens.json` (DTCG) when one exists, so a person picks `color.accent`, not a hex; the arg is written as the token's name and the component resolves it. Without a tokens file, a plain control.
151	3. **§5.7 design systems**: the agentic design-system build writes its tokens as a DTCG file and generates the CSS from it, instead of CSS alone. One-line change to §5.7's "The artifact" bullet.
152	
153	## 10. What this replaces in CawCo today
154	
155	Cutover, one path, the old one deleted:
156	
157	| Today | Under C |
158	|---|---|
159	| D29 text: "Svelte only", "No dev server for the agent to keep alive", compile location "the owner's pick" | Every toolchain in §2's table; the **daemon** keeps the toolchain alive; the compile runs in the workspace, settled |

A mocked screen is a real screen component plus a sheet. OpenUI stays only for agent-made data views (option D's remit: "Ask Caw for a view", blocks). §5.7's "Mockups" bullet is rewritten to point at sheets. |

170	## 11. Ready to paste
171

**What the "CawCo plugin" is.** When the daemon starts a project's dev server (Vite, Astro, Nuxt or Next), it passes in a small piece of CawCo code through that server's own start function. That's how Storybook adds itself too. Nothing is installed into the project and its config files aren't edited. The code does three jobs:
1. It serves the sheet page, which mounts each story of a component side by side with the project's real CSS, fonts and tokens. Without it the dev server only serves the app's own routes, and the agent ends up writing a dev route into the app to show variants. That's the 15,000-line card defect.
2. It stamps `file:line:column` onto elements for React, Vue and the others. Svelte provides this itself in dev, so there it isn't needed.
3. It sends compile errors to the agent with their line.

**Why Angular and plain webpack are the exception.** Their dev servers have no way to accept that code at start without editing the project's `angular.json` or webpack config. Fable's fallback ("run their dev script, pins without a source line") would give them no sheet page at all, because the plugin is what serves it. So it adds nothing beyond the normal app preview they already have. The result: those projects keep the regular preview of their running app, with pins on elements, and live component sheets say plainly that their toolchain isn't supported. There's no fallback path, so there's nothing for you to authorise.

## Scope
- `scripts/probe-kit/specs/**`: 122 spec files, one added per fix over the last weeks and never pruned.

## Method: a static audit; don't run the suite
Running all 122 specs is exactly the repeated CI he objects to.

For each spec and each rig proof, find:
1. **What it asserts**, in one line.
2. **Why it was added:** the commit that introduced it (`git log --diff-filter=A --format='%h %s' -- <file>`) and the failure it was written to catch.
3. **Whether that behaviour still exists on main:** grep for the code it exercises; a removed feature makes its spec dead.
4. **Whether another spec or check proves the same thing:** same assertions, or a superset.
5. **Whether it can run at all:** e.g. it needs a scratch fleet, which can't start inside a workspace; that's fine if it runs on the host.
6. **Whether it is known to fail on main for a reason unrelated to the product.** Known so far:
