work-items.ts `checkOnce` wraps `runChecks` for all three stages: finish_item's checks ("at finish_item"), the recheck after a rebase ("after the rebase") and the land gate ("in the land gate"). A check is skipped when the same command passed on the exact tree the workspace holds now (same `expect` if it has one), or when a covering command did. Every other check runs. Passes live in memory per item: `passes: Map<item, Map<tree, Passed[]>>`, cleared in `finish`. A hub restart runs everything again.

The tree comes from `treeOf`: `left=$(git status --porcelain, outputs excluded) && test -z "$left" && git rev-parse --verify 'HEAD^{tree}'`, plus `git hash-object` of the item's outputs when it has any. A dirty workspace gives no tree, so nothing is recorded or skipped. A pass is kept only if the tree is the same before and after the run. A different tree never skips.

### New

- Caw has a dock beside the project page. Press Caw in the project's header to open it. It shows the same thread a thread tab does, starts an empty thread on the project's starter cards, and has a menu of your threads. Caw's settings moved to the header's ⋯ menu.
- The task sheet now shows what a task produced. The attempt's report comes first, then each output as what it is: documents, tables, pages and pictures, never a list of file names. Each attempt says how it went in plain words, with Try again when nothing is running, and its session's transcript can open into a pane of its own.
- Pausing a machine now also stops the commands already running there, and runs them again when the pause ends. A workflow says when its command is waiting for a pause to end.

### Improved

- Two panes side by side no longer slow the dashboard down. Switching tabs takes about a quarter of the time it did, and a streaming reply costs the same as it does in one pane.
- Sessions start lighter: CawCo's tools load upfront only where a session uses them every turn.
- A fleet skill keeps updating after you add your own notes to it or it builds Python caches. Only a change to a file the fleet sent counts as an edit, and an update keeps everything else in the folder.
- A fleet plugin's files stay in place while its hooks run, and the plugin is sent again only when it changed.
- A fleet change an agent asks you to approve now says why it wants it, shows only what changes (before and after, with project names) and what it affects, and for an install, how old the source is and its stars or downloads. Agents can also list their own artifacts and see which ones are waiting on someone.

### Fixed

- A session keeps the effort you chose through a crash, a restart, an account move or a continue. Before, one relaunch could drop it back to medium for good.
- In iPhone Safari, the areas behind the status bar and toolbar take the dashboard's own colours at the top and bottom, in light and dark, with a drawer or sheet open too.
- A session's instructions hold for its whole life, and restarting a delegate from the dashboard keeps it a delegate.
- A spent workspace that a preview still shows is kept until that preview is removed.

## Cause

What held the items: the landing queue, packages/hub/src/landing.ts:217 (before this change):
```ts
return await deps.queue(`${deps.repo ?? start.remote}#${base}`, () => attempt(base, deps, 1));
```
There is one landing at a time per project#main. The landing in its turn runs fetch, rebase, the **recheck of the item's checks** (Apple gate included, on the Mac's single heavy-run slot) and the land gate. Every item whose checks had passed waited behind it. Nothing told those items' checkQueue: only `runChecks`' `asCheck` slot and pause waits ever set it.

Per item, from the parent's readings (obelisk, ~00:10Z):
- **cca4f329 / 8a22907f, d654eac4 / ddc28979, a4e27882 / ff8686f1**: touch no Apple path, nothing running in the workspace, no rebase after checking_since. A rebase happens only inside the turn (`attempt`). So their checks had passed and they were waiting in the cockpit#main landing queue.
- **678d8943 / 3f262cba, 0a6da208 / 11b83cd1, 675f4b6d / 4ac436b1**: they touch Apple paths, but no build-both or heavy-run process of theirs is on the Mac, and none was rebased. Their first-run checks had ended and they wait in the same queue. Not ruled out: one could instead be stuck in its Mac check-workspace setup (`call` bundle / workspaceAt).
- **188c7ddb / 153fd0db**: same queue; it has since landed.
- **3003f5e9**: the only one with words. It was waiting on the Mac's heavy slot itself, most likely as the turn holder's recheck after its rebase. The slot was held by check workspace 12e6d417's compile, which is why that has no work_items row. It has since landed.
- **0ecf4bf8 / 01960ff3 (Mac)**: not waiting. Its Apple gate is compiling and holds the Mac's slot (pid 74943).

No slot was leaked (heavy-run slots are flock locks the kernel frees). Every check that was meant to run did run. The fault was a wait that named nothing.

Two more silent waits in the same flow, now covered:
- the agent's per-folder line (session.ts `dispatch`, `key = command:${cwd}`): a command queued behind another in its workspace;
- `ensureBoundary` before spawn (workflow-command.ts `runWorkflowCommand`), and the hub's landing and git commands, which carried no `onWait`.

## Fix (3 commits on top of origin/main 637609a44)
- **landing.ts**: `landingQueue` tracks the landing running and those waiting, per key. Each waiter's `turn.onWait` gets `queued to land on main behind “title” (id8) and N more`, re-told whenever the head changes, and null when its turn starts. `LandingDeps.turn` is passed by `land` and `pushBranch`.

## Capture Build and Test Diagnostics

Before the next necessary build or test, resolve `tools/axbuild` under the **actual loaded package** in Claude Code (`command -v axbuild`; if that finds nothing, `tools/axbuild` two levels above the `Base directory for this skill:` path of a loaded Axiom skill) or Codex (`<plugin-root>/tools/`), or discover an executable on PATH in Pi. Check executable permission and run its absolute path with `--help`; assign that observed path to `AXBUILD`. Never infer an installation path from an example.

Cursor and MCP distributions do not bundle axbuild and expose no axbuild MCP wrapper. Use the **saved-log fallback** below when a verified shell helper is unavailable.

Before **every** Xcode invocation, run `pgrep -lx xcodebuild; echo "pgrep exit=$?"`: exit 1 means none are running, 0 lists them, and any other exit means the inventory failed. Investigate existing builds; process count and age do not establish zombie status. Never terminate unrelated processes. When interrupted or timed out, axbuild also stops build scripts and other processes descended from its build that Xcode moved into separate process groups, found by parentage when cleanup begins and on each cleanup pass. It reports `cleanup-incomplete` for any such descendant it could not stop or verify (another user's, unreadable, or being debugged). Jobs that had already left the build's process tree, such as daemons or launchd-started tools, are neither stopped nor reported. Inspect ownership before stopping anything it lists. Discover the actual scheme and destination before executing:

```bash
"$AXBUILD" xcodebuild -scheme "$SCHEME" -destination "$DESTINATION" build
"$AXBUILD" swift test --package-path "$PACKAGE"
```

Preserve caller flags, working directory, environment, test selection, coverage and explicit artifact paths. The wrapper adds absent diagnostic defaults; it never cleans caches or automatically rebuilds. Do not pipe a build through another command.

Inspect `command` (native outcome) and `collection` (evidence completeness) separately. Native success can accompany partial collection. The default JSON is bounded to 8,000 UTF-8 bytes; inspect `omissions` and read `artifacts.report` relative to the absolute `artifacts.run` directory for complete records and evaluated values. The startup stderr JSON identifies the run directory before completion. Use diagnostic locations and values rather than rebuilding to redisplay output.

The retained log is the primary compiler source; test results and validated Swift Testing events supplement it. A null failed-test count means uncertainty, not zero. Preserve result bundles for attachment export, coverage, console logs and deeper inspection. Native informational commands pass their output through.

**Saved-log fallback:** redirect the necessary native command's stdout/stderr to a unique file, let it finish, record its exit status and inspect that saved file. An xcresult build summary is not equivalent to the compiler log. Read an existing log before considering another build. If a build's output ends in a truncation marker, or before xcodebuild's closing `** BUILD … **` or `** TEST … **` line, read the saved log or report instead of rebuilding.

When building on macOS based CI hosts you can use the command-line tool `xcodebuild`.

SwiftPM records the result of dependency resolution in `Package.resolved` (at the top-level of the package) and it's used when performing dependency resolution (rather than having SwiftPM searching the latest eligible version of each package). Title: Safely pinning SPM dependencies to exact versions
URL: https://www.polpiella.dev/safely-pinning-spm-depedencies-to-exact-versions
Published: 2023-02-15T00:00:00.000Z
Author: N/A
Highlights:
As package resolution is a step of the build process, there is no easy and automated way of installing all Swift Package Manager dependencies into a vendor directory and committing it to source control like we do with CocoaPods.

For this reason, we decided to go for the next best option we had to ensure reproducible builds, which was pinning dependencies to exact versions and committing the `Package.resolved` file to source control.
...
When you add a Swift Package Manager dependency to an Xcode project or to a Swift package or Xcode project within an `.xcworkspace`, the swift build system will generate/update a `Package.resolved` file under `<workspace_name>.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`. This file will contain information about the version, revision and URL of all dependencies used by the project.

The way `Package.resolved` differs from more traditional lock file implementations is that when something changes in your Swift Package Manager dependencies, the `Package.resolved` file will automatically update to reflect this during a build. That being said, if you decide to depend on a specific version of a package, this `Package.resolved` file shouldn’t really change during a build but, when we did some tests, we uncovered a potential risk we wanted to mitigate before switching our third-party dependencies over to Swift Package Manager:

Swift Package Manager relies on source control to resolve dependencies, which means that when you specify a version in your `Package.swift`, all you’re saying is that you want to check out a specific git tag. Now, if someone decided to re-tag the version of a package you depend on to point to a different commit (with all the implications that could have), the build system would update the `Package.resolved` file to reflect this change the next time you build your app.

While you would be able to tell that there’s been a change locally if you track the `Package.resolved` file under source control, this can be a big problem for CI builds, as you wouldn’t be able to tell if there’s been any changes. Imagine the scenario where one of your third-party dependencies has re-tagged a release to a different commit (which hasn’t been tested and is different from what you’re expecting) and your release pipeline picks it up in the build that’s going out to your users 😱.
...
After adding the dependency to the project and specifying its version rule to be exactly `1.0.0`, the generated `Package.resolved` file looks like this:
...
```
{
  "pins" : [
    {
      "identity" : "testspmpackage",
      "kind" : "remoteSourceControl",
      "location" : "https://github.com/polpielladev/TestSPMPackage.git",
      "state" : {
        // This is the commit sha that the v1.0.0 tag points to
        // 👇
        "revision" : "c959141bd7a39740f91e7e7431bb6d56ad84e4f6",
        "version" : "1.0.0"
      }
    }
  ],
  "version" : 2
}
...
We commit this file to source control and push it to our remote repository.

Let’s now consider the scenario where someone decides to change the `v1.0.0` tag’s commit to a different one with sha `48c496db8ecd8e12277ad27db7c2a92fd5f93438`. Next time we build the app, there will be a change to the `Package.resolved` file:
...
```
{
...
pins" : [
    {
...
identity" : "testspmpackage",
      "kind" : "remoteSourceControl",
      "location" : "https://github.com/polpielladev/TestSPMPackage.git",
      "state" : {
        // This is the NEW commit sha that the v1.0.0 tag points to
        // 👇
        "revision" : "48c496db8ecd8e12277ad27db7c2a92fd5f93438",
        "version" : "1.0.0"
      }
    }
  ],
  "version" : 2
}
...
would show up in our `git diff` and we would get the chance to confirm whether we are ... or we want to investigate the change further before proceeding ... still build fine and ship our app
...
Luckily, there is a flag built-in to `xcodebuild` which allows us to mitigate this risk. Passing `-disableAutomaticPackageResolution` to the `xcodebuild` command tells the build system to not update the `Package.resolved` file if any of the dependencies have changed and, if it can’t resolve all packages with the information provided by `Package.resolved`, then fail the build.

```
xcodebuild
  -workspace SomeWorkspace.xcworkspace                                          \
  -scheme Debug                                                                 \
  -configuration Debug                                                          \
  -derivedDataPath ./derived_data/                                              \
  # 👇
  -disableAutomaticPackageResolution                                            \
  -sdk 'iphonesimulator'                                                        \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=6C6A5129-4D65-4A35-A439-67C894B4FF65' \
  -enableCodeCoverage YES                                                       \
  build-for-testing
...
Even better, if you are using fastlane, you can set this flag by passing true to the `disable_package_automatic_updates` parameter in both the gym and scan actions 🎉:
...
```
run_tests(
  workspace: SomeWorkspace.xcworkspace,
  scheme: 'Debug',
  clean: true,
  device: 'iPhone 14',
  configuration: 'Debug',
  sdk: 'iphonesimulator',
  derived_data_path: './derived_data/',
  reset_simulator: true,
  build_for_testing: true
  # 👇
  disable_package_automatic_updates: true
)

## Package.resolved and pinning

 The version requirement in the manifest is a range; the version resolved from it is recorded in `Package.resolved`. That file is your lockfile: it names the exact version and commit hash each dependency resolved to, including transitive ones. It belongs in version control, and CI must build from it rather than re-resolving. 

```
// Package.resolved (excerpt) — the source of truth for what actually built
{
  "pins" : [
    {
      "identity" : "swift-collections",
      "location" : "https://github.com/apple/swift-collections.git",
      "state" : {
        "revision" : "94cf62b3ba8d4bed62680706383...",   // → exact commit
        "version" : "1.1.4"                              // → exact version
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```
# Update one dependency on purpose (not the whole graph)
xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies   # → resolves to Package.resolved as-is
swift package update swift-collections    # → bumps only that pin, rewrites the lockfile

# In CI: never let resolution drift. Fail if the lockfile would change.
swift package resolve
git diff --exit-code Package.resolved     # → non-zero exit = drift; CI fails
...
Tip: commit `Package.resolved` from the workspace (`.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`) for app projects, or the root one for standalone packages. Reproducible builds (covered in Build System) depend on it.
...
```

Here comes the catch: This approach does not work on our Jenkins CI. I don’t know what I’m doing wrong here, but the xcodebuild command line tool won’t notice something changed on the develop branch of the SDK and would checkout the older revision.
...
I removed Package.resolved from git index and added it to .gitignore so after the git clone/checkout there should be no Package.resolved file
...
org.swift.swift ... org.swift
...
’re using Fastlane ... I am also explicitly setting the cloned ... to make sure the cloned ... are deleted on workspace clean ... up via cloned_source_packages_
...
The generated xcodebuild command by Fastlane looks like this: $ xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies -scheme ScannerShowcase -project ScannerShowcase.xcodeproj -configuration Release -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath SourcePackage
...
I'd expect that if I delete all that cached packages and not having any Package.resolved file present xcodebuild would resolve the swift package to the latest revision available. Instead it seems there still is something cached somewhere and xcodebuild is using that cache.
...
As it turns out there seems to be now way to achieve the same results with xcodebuild command line tool as with Xcode's Update Package or Update to Latest Versions.
The command line tools rely on data stored inside derived data while updating packages. Thanks to Gregory Higley's answer here I was able to solve the issue by deleting the derived data for that specific build job by

Keeping Showcase.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved out of git index,
adding Package.resolved to .gitignoreto keep it that way,
and adding the following stage to the declarative pipeline inside the Jenkins file:

stage('Clean up') {
 steps {
 script { env.DERIVED_DATA_PATH=sh(returnStdout: true, script: "xcodebuild -showBuildSettings | grep -m 1 BUILD_DIR | grep -oE \"/.*\" | sed 's|/Build/Products||'") }
 echo "Derived data path is: ${env.DERIVED_DATA_PATH}"
 // The above will return a folder with a name like /Users/you/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyProject-ehdkocavaenextdcrsaszjdmyssx
 sh script: "rm -rf ${env.DERIVED_DATA_PATH}", label: "Removing derived project data ..."
 }
}

Any other step I mentioned when asking the question wasn't necessary to achieve my goal:

No need to remove ~/Library/Cache/org.swift.swiftpm nor ~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm
No need to delete any prior created workspace on the build node
No need to to explicitly specify the SPM cloned source packages path via Fastlane with. cloned_source_packages_path: "SourcePackages"

Highlights:

...
Swift Apps (iOS, macOS)

- Have a`*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` file defining dependency version rules (among other project stuff)
- Have a`*.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved` file with the "pins" for specific package versions actually used Interactions are mostly through Xcode manually editing version rules and clicking at Update to Latest Package Versions
...

I think that would work, but may break those "dependency version rules" defined at`*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`.

So, I think first of all we'd need a specification for these dependency version rules.

[Report from delegate cockpit-579bdd72#d30ac72d — turn complete]
Headline: The Apple gate now compiles in one warm build root shared by every item, arm64 only, building once. On this Mac a one-file Swift change gates in 40 s and an openapi.json-only change in 140 s, against ~176 s quiet or ~300 s loaded before. A broken commit compiled right after a good one still fails. Typecheck and lint pass.

## Where one gate run's ~300 s went (measured once on Omars-MacBook-Pro, inside the same heavy-run and Mac build slots the gate takes)
Mechanism, quoted:
- Hub: `checkWorkspace` (packages/hub/src/work-items.ts:3570) keeps one check workspace per *source* workspace: "It stays between runs, so a build there is incremental; it is archived with `workspace`." Every new delegate workspace therefore gets a new check clone at `~/.worktrees/cockpit-<id8>` (agent workspace.ts:313).
- build-both.sh: `BUILD=$(basename "$ROOT")` and `DD="$5/$BUILD/DerivedData"`, so each new check clone means a new, empty DerivedData. 15 such roots were on disk, each 4.9 GB, 1.1 GB of it `SourcePackages`.
- No `Package.resolved` is committed, and the boundary can't reach `~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm` ("Operation not permitted"), so every new root clones all 8 packages from GitHub again.
- `-destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator"` has no active arch, so Xcode compiled x86_64 as well as arm64 (1223 `SwiftCompile normal x86_64` lines in one log).
- `--compile-only` built the generic destination twice: `ios` and then `ios 'iOS 18.5'`. The second was a null build of 8–12 s.

Timings (harness, quiet machine):
- workspace rsync 0.5 s; XcodeGen 0.0–0.1 s
- SwiftPM resolve/fetch, cold: 45.5 s and 47.2 s
- compile, cold, both archs: 129.0 s (SwiftCompile CPU 738 s); cold, arm64 only: 87.8 s (CPU 388 s)
- null build: 15.2 s with both archs, 10.3 s arm64
- warm, `openapi.json`-only change: 109.7 s. The generator re-emits 8.6 MB of Swift (`Types+Operations.swift` 4.4 MB, `Types+Components+Schemas.swift` 2.2 MB, `Client.swift` 1.8 MB), and CawCoAPI plus its dependents recompile. That cost belongs to the change itself.
- warm, one-file Swift change: 18.1 s
- slot wait in my runs: 174 s, then 2–12 min per run, behind other items' cold `--compile-only` gates and a probe-kit run

Today's per-item path is therefore resolve plus a cold both-arch compile: ~176 s quiet, the reports' 301–308 s under load. That holds whether the item is openapi-only or touches Swift.

## Fix (build-both.sh layer, which owns the DerivedData key)
- New `build-both.sh ios --gate`: compiles exactly as `--compile-only` does, but in one build root, `gate`, that every item's gate shares. The existing `rsync -rlpD --checksum --delete` makes the root's apps/apple the item's tree exactly: a changed file is written anew, an unchanged one keeps its mtime. Xcode's incremental build and SwiftPM's checkouts in that DerivedData do the rest; no cache of our own.
- `gate` is added to `LIVE`, so retirement never removes it. The per-root lock wait now prints `CAWCO-QUEUE wait build:` / `held build`, so a second gate queued on the shared root keeps its check clock still.
- Generic simulator compiles pass `ARCHS=arm64`. The Mac's simulators are Apple silicon, and no Swift source branches on `arch(`.

From cockpit-0a6da208 (find engine, landed at 0d5aea8db). Correction to my report's finding 2 ("Ctrl+K did not open Jump … not investigated"). I've now investigated it, and it's a real product bug.

Reproduced on a scratch fleet with the built dashboard on /session/<id>:
- Focus on the dashboard: Ctrl+K opens Jump, and focus lands in .jump-field.

From cockpit-0a6da208 (shell shortcuts inside artifacts). Two findings that bear on the ruling. I need one decision before I build; nothing is edited yet.

1) Under "never preventDefault from the overlay, decide with setTimeout 0", Chrome runs its own Ctrl+K.
- Chrome's help page (support.google.com/chrome/answer/157179), Windows & Linux: "Search from anywhere on the page: Ctrl + k or Ctrl + e". Chrome hands a key to the page first and runs its own shortcut only when the page didn't prevent the default. A task-later decision is too late to stop it.
- So on Linux and Windows, Ctrl+K inside an artifact would open Jump and Chrome's address-bar search at once. The focus would go to the address bar, not Jump's field. macOS lists no ⌘K binding.
- Chrome's Ctrl+Shift+N (incognito) is reserved and never reaches any page, the dashboard included. That's today's behaviour too.

Proposal (one line): keep "the page gets first claim", but decide synchronously at the very end of dispatch. On a shell combo, the overlay's window capture listener removes and re-adds a window bubble listener. That listener then runs after every listener the page registered. It reads event.defaultPrevented; only if the event is unhandled does it call preventDefault and post the forwarded message.
- Source: DOM Standard, invoke (dom.spec.whatwg.org): "Let listeners be a clone of event's currentTarget attribute value's event listener list. This avoids event listeners added after this point from being run." The clone is taken at each phase's invoke, so a listener added during window's capture phase is in window's bubble-phase clone.
- A page that handles the key itself (preventDefault, or stopPropagation, which also keeps our bubble listener from running) keeps it.
- The overlay calls preventDefault only for a combo the page left unhandled. That is what keeps Chrome's search from running alongside Jump.
- Alternative if you keep the task-later rule: Jump opens, but Chrome's address-bar search takes the focus on Linux and Windows.

2) Excalidraw claims ⌘K on every canvas, with or without a selection.
- Its ActionManager.handleKeyDown matches on keyTest alone: `filter(s=>…s.keyTest&&s.keyTest(o,…))`, then `o.preventDefault(),o.stopPropagation()`. The hyperlink action's keyTest is `e=>e[y.CTRL_OR_CMD]&&e.key===y.K`; its one-element predicate isn't checked on this path.
- Under your ruling, a canvas therefore keeps ⌘K with nothing selected as well. Your spec line "with nothing selected, Jump opens" would fail, and the honest assertion is "a canvas keeps ⌘K".
- ⌘⇧N and ⌘\ aren't bound by Excalidraw, so they still reach the shell from a canvas.

Decide 1 (synchronous end-of-dispatch, as proposed, or task-later as ruled). For 2, confirm the canvas assertion becomes "⌘K stays Excalidraw's; ⌘\ (when 2+ are open) or ⌘⇧N reaches the shell".

Both findings hold, and the leaf's fix for the first is the better design.

1. **Decide at the end of dispatch:** the DOM Standard quote backs it. Each phase takes a clone of the listener list, so a bubble listener added during window's capture phase runs after every listener the page registered. That keeps "the page gets first claim" without letting Chrome's own Ctrl+K address-bar search run alongside Jump on Linux and Windows.
2. **Excalidraw:** it matches ⌘K on the key alone, so a canvas keeps ⌘K whether or not anything is selected. The assertion changes to match.

**The rule: the page gets first claim**
- The shell takes one of its combos only when the page left it unhandled, and never from inside a field.
- The overlay's window capture listener re-adds a window bubble listener, `leftToShell` in packages/agent/src/preview-overlay/page.ts. That listener runs after every listener the page has. The code quotes the DOM Standard (https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener-invoke): "Let listeners be a clone of event's currentTarget attribute value's event listener list. This avoids event listeners added after this point from being run."
- If the event isn't defaultPrevented at that point, the overlay calls preventDefault and posts `cawco:shortcut`. Preventing it stops Chrome's own Ctrl+K from running beside Jump. Chrome help (support.google.com/chrome/answer/157179): "Search from anywhere on the page: Ctrl + k or Ctrl + e".
- Accepted edges: a page that stops propagation keeps the key, and so does one that adds its own window bubble listener in the same dispatch.
- Chrome's reserved Ctrl+Shift+N never reaches any page, the dashboard included. That is unchanged.

- Shortcut list: `@cawco/core/shell-shortcuts`.

- Action: `runShellShortcut` in shell-shortcut.ts. Shell's own keydown, PreviewPane and CanvasStages all call it. It marks the press as a key via `barGlass.byPointer`, so a forwarded Jump stands open at once.
- Unchanged: Shell's field exception, its conditional preventDefault, its ⇧ handling, and the plain-letter PANE_KEYS forwarding.

- AppDelegate.swift:118-121 registers all four combos as main-menu key commands.
- UIKit processes app key commands before WebKit does. WebKit changeset 240742: "UIKit's event processing precedence of interpreting key events for system text editing commands and app commands before dispatching unhandled key events to WebKit … UIKit now processes the event first".

artifacts/srt-eval/run-mac-checks.sh
#!/bin/bash
# The macOS workspace boundary's checks, against the Seatbelt profile this
# checkout generates from the workspace policy (packages/agent/src/boundary-policy.ts).
# Run on the Mac from an UNSANDBOXED shell in a checkout of this branch: a
# shell inside a CawCo workspace is itself under Seatbelt, which does not nest
# (srt #67: "sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted").
#
#   bash artifacts/srt-eval/run-mac-checks.sh SOURCE_REPO OTHER_REPO_ENV [SWIFT_PACKAGE] [XCODE_DIR XCODE_SCHEME]
#
# SOURCE_REPO is a git repository to cut the workspace from (~/anbar), and
# OTHER_REPO_ENV a secret file of another repository. SWIFT_PACKAGE (a dir
# in the clone, e.g. AnbarKit) gets `swift build`; XCODE_DIR and XCODE_SCHEME
# (a dir in the clone and a scheme, or `auto` for the dir's first scheme) get
# a simulator `xcodebuild build`, after `xcodegen generate` when the dir has a
# project.yml and no project (CawCo's own app: `~/cockpit OTHER_REPO_ENV ''
# apps/apple CawCo`). Each of those, git push and Playwright is a
# working row: a failure fails the run, as an OPEN escape row does.
# It starts its own sessiond on a scratch socket, creates one workspace through
# the product code (rig-workspace.ts), runs everything through the workspace's
# executor, then archives the workspace and stops what it started.
set -u
source_repo=$1 other_env=$2 swift_package=${3:-} xcode_dir=${4:-} xcode_scheme=${5:-}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
checkout=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
# The agent service's PATH has these first (packages/cli/src/service.ts `servicePath`).
export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH
# A workspace's gh and git get their token from the executor alone.
unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
export CAWCO_SESSIOND_ENDPOINT=$scratch/sessiond.sock

## Root cause
The failure ("37ms … our code 0ms") was the engine. Headless WPE composites every frame of the open in software GL: Mesa llvmpipe runs one thread per core ("The default value is the number of CPU cores present", https://docs.mesa3d.org/envvars.html) and a frame waits for the slowest thread.
- At rest the page composites nothing and never drops a frame.
- An open costs about 3s of compositing CPU, against about 80ms more on the main thread.
- A blank page's frames stall to 63ms quiet and 225ms under load.
- LP_NUM_THREADS set to 1 or 4 does not cure it.
- The page's own work in wall time also stretches with load: a 10ms Svelte flush took 67ms.

## Changes (rebased onto main: ca8b2386, a4ea1d95, 626061fb, d8681010, a1ab4ae9)
1. **New kit instrument, `scripts/probe-kit/cpu.ts` + `cpu-worker.ts`.** It reads the WebKit web process's main-thread CPU per frame interval from schedstat ("time spent on the cpu (in nanoseconds)", https://docs.kernel.org/scheduler/sched-stats.html), sampled every 0.25ms on a worker.
   - WebKit's 1ms-floored page clock (Performance.cpp `timePrecision { 1_ms }`, `std::floor`) is aligned to the sampler by bounding round trips.
   - Each window is bracketed by grain plus kernel tick (CONFIG_HZ, read from the kernel config) and capped at the interval as the page reads it, so it is never charged more than the old check read.
   - The web process is named by dominance over the other descendant processes during a busy page task.
   - Raster (SkiaCPUWorker) and compositing CPU are reported per open.
   - `attribute` also times setInterval callbacks and `on…` handlers.
2. **webkit-caw:** the 25ms limit is unchanged and now applies to the page's main-thread CPU per interval. A new assertion checks that the rehearsal ran unseen.
3. **Product: GlassCard's unseen first open is now a whole rehearsal.** The card opens, grows, shuts and folds once after load, invisible and inert, with focus left in place.
   - Its join is its own (`rehearsalJoined`). It arms the morph and never touches the shared `barGlass.joined`; touching it had broke the caw-notices bench's seam, fixed in 626061fb.
   - A real open during the rehearsal ends it and takes the join over.

   - Bisect for the cold work: inert, grow, three placings, the smile clip and a join layer did nothing. A keyboard open, or a full grow with the join armed, did. The cold work was the open with the join armed, not anything drawn.

delegate-tray is my one failing gate, and fixing it needs your decision because DESIGN.md is involved.

The two failing assertions check every cut `.title` / `.note` in apps/dashboard/src/lib/cawco/transcript/DelegateTray.svelte (lines ~1281 and ~1289). The spec, scripts/probe-kit/specs/web/delegate-tray.ts:174, says `ellipsed = !cut || (s.overflowX === "hidden" && s.textOverflow === "ellipsis")`. The product has `overflow: clip; text-overflow: ellipsis`.

The geometry part of the same assertion passes for every chip: the text sits inside the chip and before its glyph, e.g. "text 390–452 in chip 360–480, glyph at 457". Only the `overflowX === "hidden"` test fails.

The commit that broke it: 91ec2bb00 ("Words beside a mark stand on its middle: the mark line trims them to their x-height", 2026-10-16). It changed both rules from `overflow: hidden` to `overflow: clip`. 99e56fc00 then made that law in DESIGN.md's Mark Line Rule: "A run that truncates clips with `overflow: clip`, never `hidden`, which Gecko does not trim." Its comment in app.css adds: "Gecko does not trim a scroll container, so a hidden run stays 1.25px low there."

The ellipsis is not lost. WebKit bug 258265 ("`text-overflow: ellipsis` doesn't work with `overflow: clip`") is RESOLVED FIXED, landed as 265445@main in June 2023. That report already said it "works in all other major browsers (Chrome, Edge, and Firefox)". So every engine draws the ellipsis under `clip`.

To make it pass as written, I'd need one of these:
(A) Spec: line 174 accepts `overflowX` of `hidden` or `clip`. This is not a looser threshold: it is the same requirement (a non-visible overflow that draws the ellipsis), and it matches the design rule.
(B) Product: back to `overflow: hidden` on `.title` / `.note`. That breaks the Mark Line Rule: tray labels sit 1.25px low in Gecko.
I recommend A. Your brief said the gate keeps delegate-tray as it is and to STOP on a design-change cause, so it's your call.

1	# Task sheet screenshot review (iOS app vs web dashboard)
2	
3	**Verdict: FIX** — three things would embarrass the owner on his phone or iPad (transcript text running under timestamps and clipping, raw backticks showing in code text, an unreadable Page output in dark mode). Everything else is polish.
4	
5	Captures: `/home/bewinxed/.local/share/cawco/projects/70ac3d41-5a28-4a31-8e9e-3be2b03d1516/assets/task-sheet-captures/`. All 16 app frames were read against their web pair, except `web-iPad-sheet-dark` (live and seeded), which I did not open; the web light pair and the web dark expanded frames cover the same web styling. 6	
7	## Findings
8	
9	### Blocks TestFlight
10	
11	1. **Transcript prose rows do not wrap; they run under the timestamp and clip at the right edge.**
12	   - Files: `live/iPhone-sheet-light.png`, `live/iPhone-sheet-dark.png`, `live/iPhone-expanded-light.png`, `live/iPhone-expanded-dark.png`, `live/iPad-expanded-light.png`, `live/iPad-expanded-dark.png`. The same row is wrapped correctly in `live/web-iPad-expanded-*.png`.
13	   - Where: Transcript pane, every assistant text row that carries a time. Examples: "Gone-session and stale-sleep sweeps will ride the existi…" with "13:58" printed on top of "the exist" (iPhone sheet); "Typecheck and lint pass, and `count` now comes from the i…" with "14:07" over "from" (iPhone expanded); "Finding 2 is closed: … no longer c[14:09]s a" and "Replacing the install-as-check helper … and a run[14:06] type t" (iPad expanded).

Long sentences are cut off at the pane edge, so the content cannot be read. On the web the text wraps in a column that stops before the timestamp. 15	   - Severity: blocks TestFlight. Every real transcript hits it; it is the first thing seen on opening the transcript on the phone.
16	
17	2. **Raw markdown backticks are drawn around inline code.**
18	   - Files: `live/iPhone-sheet-dark.png` (Report: `` `runChecks` ``, `` `CheckRun { installs, outcomes }` ``, `` `InstallOutcome` ``, `` `outcomes` ``), `live/iPad-sheet-light.png`, `live/iPad-sheet-dark.png`, `live/iPad-expanded-light.png`, `live/iPad-expanded-dark.png` (Report, Description and transcript rows: `` `count` ``, `` `settleChecks` ``, `` `runChecks` ``, `` `stop_delegate` ``, `` `depsCheck` ``), `live/iPhone-expanded-light.png` and `live/iPhone-expanded-dark.png` (`` `count` ``). 21	   - Severity: blocks TestFlight. It looks like a parser bug and appears in the first paragraph of the Report.
22	
23	3. **Page output is unreadable in dark mode.**
24	   - Files: `seeded/iPad-expanded-dark.png` (Page card, top right), `seeded/iPad-sheet-dark.png` (Page card at the bottom). Web pair `seeded/web-iPad-expanded-dark.png` keeps the page white with black text.
25	   - Where: Result > Page output, the page preview surface.
26	   - What is wrong: the app paints the page surface near-black (#121212) while the page's own text stays black, so "Harbour" and "Book a berth in two taps." are almost invisible; only the blue "Out" link shows. The page is an author-supplied document and should keep a white canvas in both themes, as on the web. iPhone dark is not captured past the Data table, but the same view is used, so expect the same.
27	   - Severity: blocks TestFlight. The output looks empty in dark mode.

29	### Polish
30	
31	4. **"Jump to latest" pill covers transcript text.** `live/iPhone-sheet-light.png`, bottom of the transcript card: the pill sits across "Writing the work… / raw, queued listing", which already collides with its timestamp (finding 1). Fix 1 first, then check whether the pill needs more bottom margin from the last row.

33	5. **Home indicator overlays content with no bottom inset.** `live/iPhone-sheet-light.png` (Description text "queued behind owns overlaps" has the indicator bar across it), `seeded/iPhone-sheet-light.png` and `-dark.png` (table header "Time / Text" crossed), `live/iPad-expanded-light.png` and `-dark.png` (right-pane Description text). This is normal while scrolling, but the sheet body should end with the safe-area inset so the last line can scroll clear of the bar. I could not tell from the frames whether it does.
34	
35	6. **Fact value column in the Data output sits at the pane midpoint.** `seeded/iPhone-sheet-light.png`, `seeded/iPhone-sheet-dark.png`, `seeded/iPad-sheet-light.png`, `seeded/iPad-sheet-dark.png`; Result > Data card, rows "Channel X" and "Starts at 19 Oct 2026": values start at ~52% of the card (x≈476 of 920 on iPhone, x≈760 on iPad), leaving a wide hole after the label. The web uses a narrow fixed label column (values at x≈327 of 920, ≈733 on iPad). Labels are also ~2pt higher than their values in the app (baseline mismatch: "Channel" vs "X").
36	
37	7. **Light-mode transcript surface changes tone.** `seeded/iPhone-expanded-light.png`, `live/iPhone-expanded-light.png`, `seeded/iPad-expanded-light.png`: the transcript scroll area is a beige (~#F6F3EC) under a cream header (~#FDFCF8). The web transcript pane is one cream surface. Dark mode matches. Check against DESIGN.md's surface tokens; if the beige is the sunken-surface token it is intentional, otherwise align.

Facts rows themselves (Stage, Status, Labels) align on one label column at x=18 / value column at x≈222 (iPhone), matching the web.
40	
41	9. **Date copy differs from the web.** Header "Created Oct 13, 12:47 PM" (app) vs "Created Oct 13 at 12:47 PM" (web); same for "Started Oct 13, 1:54 PM" vs "Started Oct 13 at 1:54 PM". WORDS.md should say which is right.
42	
43	10. **Picture output is a ~35×22 gradient pill, not a picture.** `seeded/iPad-expanded-light.png`, `seeded/iPad-expanded-dark.png`, and `seeded/web-iPad-*`. App and web agree (parts.json `task-output-cover.png` h=72), so this is the seeded fixture image, not an app bug; mention so the owner is not surprised.

45	## Capture gaps (not defects, but not verified)
46	
47	- `live/iPhone-sheet-light.png` is scrolled to Attempts (offset 813), so the light-mode Report on iPhone is not shown; dark covers the same layout.
48	- No iPhone frame scrolls past the Data table in the seeded run. Attempts tabs (167×36), status words ("Finished in 1 min"), Try again (99×56.7) and the Page/Picture cards are only confirmed by `seeded/iPhone-parts.json` (all `shows=true`, no overlap in the frames: hint 253 wide beside the 99-wide button) and by the iPad frames.
49	- `live/web-iPhone-expanded-light.png` and `-dark.png` have an empty transcript (the web reference did not load it), so the iPhone live expanded frames have no web comparison. `seeded/web-iPhone-*` show the Time column wrapping "09:0 / 0": that is a web defect, and the app's table was not scrolled into view.
50	- In `live/iPhone-parts.json` the `says` value for `task-sheet-body` (offset 813 vs 988 in the log) confirms the frame was taken mid-scroll; no layout fault.
51	
52	## What matches well
53	
54	Part order is the same as the web in every frame: header facts, Result with the report first, then outputs in the order document, data, table, page, picture (parts.json order agrees: post.md, schedule.json, week.csv, page.html, cover.png), then Attempts with tabs, status word, "Try again" and the transcript pane. Outputs are drawn as what they are (Document, Data, Table, Page, Picture) with no file names. iPad expanded puts the transcript on the left beside the review on the right, with the header pinned and the "open in its own pane" hint, as on the web; iPhone expanded has the transcript covering the sheet with Collapse transcript and Open session. Spacing rhythm, type scale, the red section rules, and the olive "Finished in …" and yellow "Needs you" chips match the web in light and dark, and body, hint and timestamp ink stays readable in both themes.

Headline: Caw's replies now show up in the dock without a reload. The dock stopped redrawing after a thread's first message because of a scheduler bug, and that's fixed. The caw-dock check on the host passes, so his real replies render in every variant, and the iOS build compiles.

The hub was never the problem. It stores Caw's reply and sends a `thread.message` frame, and the frame reached the page in every variant. The dock just stopped redrawing.

## Trace: hub to view
- **Hub write.** Your words go into the thread when you send. Caw's plain-text answer is posted when his turn ends (`answerUnreplied`, caw.ts:808–822). A `thread_reply` and a not-woken note are posted the same way (`noteIn`, caw.ts:1035). All three go through `said` (caw.ts:875–886), which sends `thread.message` (:881) and then the thread's row (:883).
- **Stream.** `registry.broadcast` sends to every dashboard (server.ts:16617–16619, registry.ts:227).
- **Dashboard.** `handleFrame` (client.svelte.ts:2871–2879) calls `adoptThreadMessage`, which updates `state.threadMessages`. ThreadPane reads it (:146) and Transcript draws it.
- **First message of a new thread.** `startThread` creates the message list. The dock switches its pane to the new thread id in place (`docked.onthread`, CawDock.svelte:78); a thread tab is re-addressed with `workspace.retarget`. Either way the pane reads the whole thread again (`readThread`).
- **Switching threads in the dock.** Picking from the menu remounts the pane (`{#key chosen}`).

## Reproduction
In my workspace, on a scratch fleet driven by playwright-core:
- Every dock case failed: the hub's frame reached the page, but the dock never drew the message.
- Debug counters showed the cause: the scheduler bumped zero times, the dock pane re-joined on every change, and its build count stayed frozen.
- Thread tabs worked. Caw on and Caw off failed the same way.

## The cause and the fix
1. **Scheduler** (`join`). An unfocused transcript joins the rebuild scheduler from its own `$effect` (Transcript.svelte:981–993). `join` read the fingerprint inside that effect, so every session change re-ran the effect and re-joined with the new fingerprint. The tick never saw a change, so no unfocused transcript ever rebuilt after it joined. Now the fingerprint is read untracked, and a join's cleanup removes only its own registrant. This covers every unfocused transcript, not just the dock.
2. **The dock is the transcript being read.** CawDock now passes `focused`, so it rebuilds on every message and keeps up with the newest one.
3. **ThreadPane's session id follows its address**, so a pane re-addressed to a new thread no longer shares an id with the next New thread pane.
4. **A crash this exposed** (Transcript.svelte). A Transcript mounting on a session whose sizes it had saved builds during setup and read the ledger's `recorded` before it existed: `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'er' before initialization`, and the side panel's error boundary removed the dock. `recorded` now sits with the rest of the ledger's state.
5. **A message arriving during a read.** Before, a read overwrote the list with its own copy and lost any message whose frame arrived while it was in flight. Now those messages are kept after the read's messages. Fixed on the web and on iOS (Threads.swift).

## iOS
- It doesn't share the frozen-dock bug: there's no scheduler there, and `adopt` redraws directly (Threads.swift:243).
- It did share the read race, now fixed.
- The Mac check "iOS build compiles" passed at d67f5d845.

## Spec (caw-dock.ts)
- Sends from the dock's New thread with Caw off, the thread it made, a thread chosen from the menu, and New thread with Caw on. In each, Caw's reply renders within a second with his turn over and no reload.

The side panel's error boundary then took the dock down. 1	### New
2	
3	- Agents can show you real components, live. A sheet is a story file next to a component, and it runs on the project's own Vite (version 6 or newer) through the workspace's preview. Each story renders as the real component in the project's own styles. An edit redraws it in under a tenth of a second without a reload, and a change that doesn't compile shows its file, line and column over the last good render. A pin you drop on a sheet tells the agent the exact source line of what you tapped. The sheet sleeps after 30 minutes with no one looking and wakes when you open it again.
4	
5	<!-- TODO when 0a6da208's finder lands: one New entry for the finder (Go-to, Waiting for you, moments) that also says ↵ on a moment opens the conversation scrolled to that line and marked, older history paged in, a moment that's gone says so, and screen readers hear where they landed (open-at 03dfd3b29/6da1d7fd8 already on main). -->
6	
7	### Improved
8	
9	- Jump and the composer's @ now search through the hub, so every machine's sessions, threads and terminal sessions are ranked in one list: best match first, then the most recent and the ones still running, with your own words counting for more than tool output. Words match in any order, and each result says when a machine hasn't answered yet.
10	- A session or thread you mention with @ always reaches it. A bare name that matches more than one is refused, and the refusal lists each match so you can pick.
11	- A delegate whose checks have passed but is still waiting now says what for: its place in the queue to land on main and the item ahead of it, a command waiting its turn in its workspace, or a workspace still starting.
12	- Switching between conversations does about a quarter less work, in one pane or two, and each streamed message costs about a fifth less. Two panes now cost the same per message as one.
13	- Caw's first press is as quick as every later one. The glass card rehearses its open once, unseen, as the page loads.
14	- ⌘K and the dashboard's other shortcuts work while you're inside an artifact page. A page that uses the key itself keeps it, so a canvas keeps ⌘K for its link editor.
15	- Delegates that change the iOS or Mac app land much faster. The iOS compile check builds incrementally in one warm build folder, so a small Swift change takes about 40 seconds instead of about 5 minutes. It also doesn't compile again when a rebase leaves the app's files unchanged.
16	
17	### Fixed
18	
19	- Caw's reply shows in his dock as he sends it. Before, after a thread's first message the dock stopped drawing new messages until you reloaded. The same fault kept any conversation you weren't focused on (a second pane, a side panel) from showing new messages.
20	- A message that arrives while a thread is still loading is kept, on the web and in the app.
21	
22	- The iOS and Mac apps always build against the exact Swift package versions committed to the repository. Before, each new build folder could pick up newer patch releases on its own.
